text:
You've imagined this moment often enough during the past three years. Its ancient towers rising above the Black Forest, its workshops and libraries, its illustrious professors, and the promise of learning a craft that could change your life.
An artificer. A proper one. Someone who can breathe intelligence into ink and parchment, and perhaps one day create something worth more than everything you've earned so far.
But first, a less inspiring form of magic.
The administrator slides a document across his desk.
"First-term tuition, Mr. Fibonacci. Payable in advance."
You glance at the sum.
Three years of savings. A remarkable amount of effort, about to disappear with a single signature.
Apparently, the first lesson at the Academy is that miracles are expensive.

args.successText: Somehow you talk him into a modest concession. He adjusts the figure with visible regret, and you leave the desk feeling only mostly robbed.
args.failureText: He hears you out, nods once, and leaves the total exactly where it was. You pay. Miracles remain expensive.

parameters.text: You pay the full sum without protest. The stamp falls; three years of savings become a neat entry in a ledger.

text:
Professor Glützenbaum is a small, elderly gentleman with a magnificent white moustache and spectacles that seem perpetually on the verge of sliding off his nose. He surveys the classroom with unconcealed satisfaction.

"Welcome, ladies and gentlemen! Today, you begin your journey toward becoming artificers. A noble profession, requiring intelligence, precision, patience, and a truly unreasonable tolerance for failure."

He produces a playing card from his pocket and places it on the lectern. The card promptly scuttles across the wood, stops at the edge, turns around, and comes back.

"Observe! A piece of cardboard that obeys instructions. Remarkable, isn't it? And this is merely a child's toy compared to the enchantments you may one day create."

He catches the card before it escapes again.

"But first, the foundations. All artificery draws upon four fundamental magical essences."

He gestures toward four colored sets of cards arranged on his desk.

"Green: life, growth, restoration, and the stubborn refusal of nature to stay properly organized."

"Blue: knowledge, perception, illusion, and the subtle art of knowing more than one ought."

"Red: energy, speed, chaos, and everything my colleagues wish I would stop demonstrating indoors."

"Black: structure, industry, preservation, and decay. The art of building things to last—or persuading them that they've lasted quite long enough."

He beams at the class.

"Each essence has its own properties, and every artificer develops particular affinities. You'll discover yours in time. For now, the Academy has kindly provided a selection of elementary decks."

He indicates the four sets.

"Choose whichever appeals to you. And don't fret over the decision! You'll study all four essences eventually."

neighbor_match.text:
Professor Glützenbaum claps his hands.

"Splendid! Now, the clever thing about these cards is that they already know how to play. They'll remember their own abilities, follow your instructions, and obey the rules without requiring a judge to inspect every move. Most of the time, anyway."

A few students laugh.

"Of course, designing such enchantments is considerably harder than using them. But we'll get to that soon enough."

He gestures toward the tables.

"For now, turn to your neighbor and have a friendly match. Experiment! Make mistakes! Discover what your cards can do!"

The young woman seated beside you turns with a warm, slightly shy smile.

"Hello! I'm Molly. Shall we give it a try?"

text:
The morning finds you in one of the Academy's artificery workshops, a curious mixture of classroom and laboratory. Rows of heavy wooden workbenches are cluttered with pigments, delicate instruments, glass vessels and mysterious brass contraptions. At the front stands Miss Lombard, a stern-looking woman in her forties, whose immaculate appearance suggests that even the dust in this room knows better than to misbehave.

"Good morning. I am Professor Lombard, and I shall be teaching you artificery. Yesterday, you learned to play with enchanted cards. Today, you shall begin learning to make them."

She pauses to let the distinction sink in.

"An artificer must be able to bind magical essences into a precise, stable creation. We shall begin with Conjuration: shaping a card from raw materials through intuition and experimentation. The result may surprise you. Indeed, you may discover enchantments you do not yet understand, which you will eventually learn to reproduce deliberately."

She picks up a blank card and places it on her desk.

"Remember: the purpose of these exercises is not merely to produce better playing cards. Every technique you master here is a step toward creating the sophisticated magical artifacts upon which our profession is built."

A young man sitting beside you leans over with a friendly smile. He has an easy confidence about him, and an accent you cannot quite place.

"She's quite right, you know. My family has been crafting enchanted objects for generations. Back home, a reliable magical advisor can fetch more than a merchant's entire cargo. And here we are, learning to make pieces of cardboard chase one another across a table."

He gives a delighted chuckle.

"Ousmane, by the way. Ousmane Tempeli. I came all this way to discover what these northern Academies know that we don't. With any luck, something worth bringing home."

Before you can reply, Miss Lombard clears her throat.

"Mr. Tempeli. I trust your conversation is contributing to the education of the entire class?"

"Not yet, Professor. But I have every confidence it will."

A few students laugh. Miss Lombard does not.

"How reassuring. Then perhaps you and Mr. Fibonacci would care to begin your work."

Ousmane gives you a cheerful wink as he turns toward his materials.

"Well, Antonio. Shall we see what wonders we can produce?"

parameters.title: Family and ambitions
parameters.description: Ousmane Tempeli is a warm, confident young man from a distinguished family of artificers in a distant southern country. He came to the Academy to discover unfamiliar techniques and bring valuable knowledge home. He has practical familiarity with the commercial world of magical artifacts.

text: Moly tells you she appreciated the way you made her feel welcome. She offers you a token of gratitude, pick your favorite!
title: Molly's gift

text: Molly finds you with an armful of notes and a shy, hopeful smile. She says she has been wanting to study together, and that she would love to share a few tricks from the green magic she knows best—if you can spare an evening at the library soon.

Molly finds you again with a shy brightness that was not there before. She says your friendship has come to mean more to her than she quite knows how to say, and she wants you to have something from her own collection—a card she has kept close. She lays a few favorites before you and asks you to choose the one that speaks to you.

Molly finds you with a hopeful bounce in her step and asks if you would like to go hiking in the Gray Mountains. She talks about the trail, the overlook, and the clear air on a bright weekend, and waits to see whether you will come along.

parameters.text: Molly's smile falters. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and says maybe another time.

text: Before long you are both on a bright weekend trail in the Gray Mountains, wind in the pines. Molly sets an easy, tireless pace while your lungs burn and your legs complain, but she never leaves you behind—slowing on the steep bits, offering a hand over the rocks, and laughing with you when you stop to catch your breath. By the overlook you are worn out and grinning, glad you said yes.

Molly seeks you out with a thoughtful look. She says she has been watching how you carry yourself, and she respects the care you put into your work. She asks if you would take on a mentoring post with her at the library on Tuesday evenings, helping younger students find their footing.

text: Molly seeks you out again, this time with a small pouch clutched in her hands. She says she has grown to respect how you work beside her, and she wants you to have something she makes herself—a strand of beads she has been stringing for you. She offers them freely, though she glances toward her dust pouch as if she would understand if you preferred something more ordinary.

Molly finds you with a tight smile that does not reach her eyes. Whatever has soured between you still sits heavy on her, and she makes no effort to hide it. She presses a small purse into your hands anyway, calling it charity for someone who clearly needs the help, and waits to see whether you will take the slight.

Molly draws you aside, cheeks flushed, and admits she has noticed the way you have been flirting with her. She does not sound angry so much as uncertain, and she asks you plainly what your intentions are—whether this is a game, or something you mean to pursue.

parameters.text: Molly's face falls. She nods a little too quickly and looks away, clearly a bit upset, before murmuring that she must have misunderstood.

text: Molly finds you with a soft, eager smile and asks if you would go out with her again—this time to the Royal Pigeon Inn. She has already thought it through: she knows coin is tight for you, so she is inviting you as her guest, and she hopes you will say yes.

Molly leans in close, voice low, and asks if you would come with her to her room at the Royal Pigeon Inn. There is no mistaking the invitation—she wants you alone with her, and she is waiting on your answer.

Molly catches your sleeve in the morning bustle and pulls you aside, a little breathless. She promised the kitchen staff she would lend a hand today, but the prep work has piled higher than she expected and she still has lessons waiting. She looks at you hopefully and asks if you would help her in the kitchens.

Molly's face falls. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and hurries off toward the kitchens alone.

text: Still warm from the kitchens, Molly tells you she really enjoyed cooking with you. With a shy, hopeful smile she proposes a pajamas night at her place—good books, hot chocolate, and nowhere else to be.

parameters.text: Molly's eyes light up. She already looks forward to pajamas, books, and hot chocolate with you.
Molly's smile falters. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and says maybe another time.

text: Evening finds you at Molly's place in pajamas, a mug of hot chocolate warming your hands and a stack of good books between you. Hours slip by in soft talk and shared pages until the hour grows late. At the door, as you prepare to leave, Molly looks up at you, waiting to see how you will say good night.

parameters.text: You lean in and kiss Molly good evening. She softens into it, cheeks warm, and murmurs a shy good night as you step into the hall.
You cheerfully thank Molly for the books, the chocolate, and the company. She beams, clearly pleased, and waves you off with a bright good night.

text: You come upon Elsa angrily reprimanding Molly in the morning hall. Elsa insists it is not befitting Molly's rank to meddle with servants, her voice sharp with wounded pride. It seems Molly tried to help the serving staff with their work, and Elsa, a proud noble, took the gesture as an affront to the order she holds dear.

parameters.text: Molly's eyes fill with tears as she shrinks back from Elsa's rebuke. Elsa softens once she sees you take her side, her anger ebbing into a stiff, satisfied calm.
Molly draws a shaky breath, then finds her courage and stands up to Elsa. Her voice is quiet but firm as she defends helping those who need it, and Elsa falls briefly silent.

text: As you greet Molly, she takes you by the hand and insists there is something you really need to do. Surprised, you follow her to a gym room lined with weights and mats. She nods toward a rack, encourages you to lift, and winks as if daring you to show her what you can do.

parameters.text: Molly stares as you hoist the weight with ease, clearly surprised by your strength.
The bar barely budges, but Molly only grins and urges you on, cheering every shaky attempt.
Molly flushes with pleasure at the compliment, clearly flattered, and demonstrates another clean lift with a shy smile.

text:
"That was fun! You're quite good at this, aren't you?"
She gathers her cards, carefully stacking them into a neat pile.
"It's funny, isn't it? All those little enchantments, just to make some cardboard follow the rules of a game. And apparently this is the easy part!"
She laughs.
"My father once met an artificer whose cards could actually give advice. Proper conversations, I mean. Imagine being clever enough to make something like that!"
title: A Friendly Face

parameters.title: Fellow student
parameters.description: Molly is a friendly, modest fellow student who seems uncertain of her academic abilities.

text:
As you go back to your room, you pass through the library. It is settling into its evening silence, except for one table that seems determined to resist the process. Three children are gathered around a young woman with kind eyes and a rather tired smile. One is struggling with a page of arithmetic, another is constructing a tower out of books, and the third is earnestly explaining why his homework was eaten by a goat.

"Well, that is unfortunate," the young woman says, apparently taking the goat's involvement quite seriously. She looks up as you approach. "Oh, hello Anotnio! I'm Molly, you remember? Are we being too loud? We can move somewhere else."

You assure her that you aren't here to complain. Relieved, she explains that the children come from families in the nearby village, and that she helps them with their lessons in the evenings. "Some of them can't afford proper schooling. It's only a little thing, really." She glances at the growing tower of books. "Though it's becoming rather more than a little thing. I have my own studies to keep up with, and there are more children coming every week."

The tower collapses with a magnificent thud. Molly closes her eyes for a moment, then patiently begins gathering the books.

"I've been thinking I should find someone to help. A fellow student, perhaps. I'd pay them, of course. It wouldn't be fair otherwise." She smiles at you. "You wouldn't happen to know anyone who might be interested?"

parameters.text:
"Well, I could help," you suggest.

Molly brightens immediately. "Really? Oh, that would be wonderful! Are you good with children?"

Before you can answer, the smallest boy looks you up and down. "Do you know your multiplication tables?"

An interview. Already.

Molly gives you an apologetic smile. "They're very thorough."

job.description: Help younger students at the library under Molly's guidance.

parameters.text:
"Actually, I know someone who might be perfect. Emma Delamain. She's brilliant, very serious about her studies, and I think she'd make an excellent teacher. Just, err... Don't tell her I said that."

"Emma Delamain?" Molly repeats thoughtfully. "I don't think we've met. Do you think she'd be interested?"

You admit that you haven't asked her.

"Well, perhaps I could speak to her sometime." Molly smiles. "Thank you, Antonio. That's very kind of you."

From beneath the table, a small voice announces that the goat has eaten another assignment.

"It sounds like a wonderful thing you're doing. I hope you find someone to help."

"Thank you." Molly's smile is warm, if a little weary. "They're good children, really. Even when they aren't being especially good."

One of the children proudly presents her with a drawing of a dragon. It has six legs, three heads, and what appears to be a very large moustache.

"Oh, that's lovely!" she says, with complete sincerity.

title: The Little Scholars

parameters.title: Village tutor
parameters.description: Molly volunteers to tutor children from poor families in the nearby village. She is kind, patient, and increasingly overwhelmed by the work.

text:
Professor Glützenbaum greets the class with his usual enthusiasm, standing behind a desk laden with enchanted cards, pigments, and an alarming assortment of delicate brass instruments.

"Good afternoon, my promising young artificers! This morning, you learned to create. This afternoon, you shall learn to improve! Or, occasionally, to make things worse in a carefully calculated and academically respectable manner."

He holds up a card depicting an armored knight.

"Augmentation! We strengthen an existing enchantment, making our creation more powerful, more resilient, or more capable. Naturally, greater power demands greater magical energy. A stronger card will generally cost more mana to play."

He sets it down and picks up another.

"Distillation! The opposite principle. We remove something from an enchantment, reducing its power but also its cost. A modest creation, efficiently designed, may prove far more useful than an extravagant masterpiece."

"Rather like certain students," someone murmurs from the back.

"Who said that?"

The sharp voice comes from a young man a few seats away. Dark-eyed, handsome, and visibly indignant, he has turned toward his neighbor, who looks utterly bewildered.

"You were looking at me."

"I was looking at the professor!"

"With that expression?"

"What expression?"

"That one!"

Professor Glützenbaum clears his throat.

"Mr. Farid, I presume? An excellent demonstration of excessive energy expenditure. Perhaps we should attempt a little distillation."

The classroom erupts in laughter. Farid's expression darkens, but he eventually folds his arms and settles back into his seat, muttering something about disrespectful northerners.

Glützenbaum returns to his cards, entirely untroubled.

"Now then! You have cards, you have tools, and you have two splendid ways to improve your decks—or ruin them beyond recognition. I suggest you begin with the former."

parameters.title: Proud and quarrelsome
parameters.description: Farid is a young student from an Arabic realm, quick to take offense and fiercely protective of his dignity. He has a fiery temperament and appears entirely willing to argue over the smallest perceived slight.

text: Before enchanting class, the academy sometimes runs a sports hour—mostly laps, and plenty of them. Across the track you spot Emma and Molly jogging side by side, chatting pleasantly as they go. Molly looks thoroughly at ease, sporty and unfazed, while Emma is clearly struggling to keep up, gasping between words as she tries to hold the conversation.

parameters.text: You compliment Molly on her shape. She beams, clearly pleased.
You compliment Emma on her figure. She scoffs—but you catch her smile.
You taunt Emma as you pass them. She smirks.

text:
Well, that's done. First year's tuition paid.

And you're broke again.

Three years of savings, gone in the time it took an administrator to stamp a piece of paper. You'd better pass those exams. Preferably with honors. Preferably without starving in the meantime.

You make your way through the crowded Academy corridor, dodging students, luggage, and an elderly professor who appears to be arguing with his own hat.

That's when you notice her.

A young woman is studying the timetable pinned to the noticeboard. First year, judging by the schedule she's examining. Like you, then.

Unlike you, she seems to know exactly what she's doing.

She turns toward the village, carrying a precarious tower of books that looks as though it might require its own structural engineer.

Naturally, you decide to offer your assistance.

A perfectly chivalrous impulse. One that has absolutely nothing to do with the long, graceful legs visible beneath her skirt.

You catch up and call out to her.

She turns.

Bright green eyes settle on you, appraising you with an intelligence that would probably be intimidating if you were currently capable of rational thought.

You should introduce yourself.

Yes. That would be sensible.

Or perhaps explain why you've stopped her.

Also sensible.

You could even try speaking. People do that, apparently.

"Take your time," she says at last, one eyebrow rising. "It's not as though I'm carrying half the Academy library."

Her expression hovers somewhere between amusement and resignation.

You have the distinct impression that this is not the first time she's had this effect on a young man.

parameters.text:
You clear your throat, summon the scattered remains of your dignity, and manage a smile.

"Sorry. I was going to ask if you needed a hand. Antonio, by the way."

"Emma. A pleasure, Antonio."

She adjusts the stack of books with surprising ease.

"And thank you, but I'm rather stronger than I look."

With a quick wink, she strides away toward the village, leaving you with the uncomfortable suspicion that she has already formed a fairly accurate opinion of you.

optionTemplates.text: A complete failure of higher reasoning

parameters.text:
This is absurd.

You've barely arrived at the Academy, and already you're being subjected to this sort of sorcery. Without warning. On the very first day.

Surely there ought to be regulations.

Nobody should be allowed to have legs like that without some sort of advance notice.

"Emma, by the way," she says, rescuing the conversation from its untimely death. "Delighted to meet you, mysterious stranger."

She sets off at a brisk pace.

A few steps later, she glances back over her shoulder.

"Oh, and one more thing..."

A mischievous smile curls at the corner of her mouth.

"The dark, silent, mysterious type? Doesn't work on me."

And with that, she disappears into the crowd.

You remain where you are for several seconds, contemplating what may well be the most spectacular conversational defeat of your academic career.

title: A Rather Unfortunate First Impression

parameters.title: First impressions
parameters.description: A striking young woman with sharp green eyes, an impressive collection of books, and an equally impressive talent for making you feel foolish. Apparently a fellow first-year student.

manualTrigger: There is a pretty girl over there!

text:
This is a risky move. Perhaps a little too aggressive? Well, fortune favors the bold. According to Henry, Emma Delamain is probably the strongest player at the Academy. After you, naturally.

You commit to the attack.

She doesn't see it coming. Victory!

Across the table, Emma realizes her mistake immediately—but a quarter of a second too late. A flash of anger crosses her delicate, heart-shaped face. Her shoulders sink, and for a brief moment she looks almost wounded. Then she straightens, gathers her composure, and meets your eyes.

"{{greeting}}Well played, Fibonacci."

She glances at the board once more, her brow furrowing. For a moment, she seems to be debating something with herself.

"Tell me. Was that a bluff, or had you calculated it from the beginning?"

parameters.text:
You conceal your considerable satisfaction and begin explaining your reasoning, starting several turns before the decisive attack. Emma listens without interrupting, her eyes moving between you and the cards still scattered across the table.

Then comes a question. A very precise question. You answer it, only to be met with another. Before long, the two of you are reconstructing the entire match, debating alternatives, and examining moves neither of you had considered at the time.

Emma's bitterness gradually disappears, replaced by intense concentration. At one point she even smiles, apparently delighted to have discovered a particularly elegant possibility. Losing, it seems, becomes considerably more tolerable when there is something interesting to learn from it.

Eventually, she rises, a little stiffly, and gathers her belongings. She regards you for a long moment, her expression thoughtful.

"Interesting, Antonio. Very interesting." A faint smile touches her lips. "Until next time."

Oh, this is too good. The Academy's brightest star, defeated by Antonio Fibonacci himself! Surely a little celebration is in order.

"Bluff? Me?" You give an extravagant shrug. "My dear Delamain, I was merely trying to give you a sporting chance."

Emma's eyes narrow. For a moment, you wonder whether you've pushed your luck.

"A sporting chance?" she repeats, very slowly.

"Well, I wouldn't want you to lose confidence. You have such a promising future."

Emma stares at you. Then, despite herself, a reluctant smile breaks through.

"How extraordinarily generous of you, Fibonacci. I shall treasure your encouragement."

She begins gathering her cards, then pauses.

"Although I do hope you're prepared for our next match."

"Naturally."

"Good. Because I intend to make you regret every single word of this conversation."

She flashes you a dazzling smile.

"And I shall be insufferably gracious about it."

Oh, no. She's waiting for an answer.

This is your chance, Antonio. You've just defeated the most formidable player at the Academy. Surely you can manage a few clever words. Something confident. Something memorable. Something that will make her look at you differently.

You open your mouth.

And then she looks at you with those eyes.

Really, this is most unfair. How is a man supposed to think under such circumstances? You had an entire strategy worked out a moment ago. Where has it gone? Perhaps it's hiding under the table.

"Well, I... that is, the thing about the attack..."

Emma raises an eyebrow. Then recognition dawns, and the corner of her mouth curls upward.

"Ah, yes. My silent admirer. I remember you."

She allows herself a small, thoroughly delighted smile.

"Well, it seems you're rather better at strategy than rhetoric."

She gathers her cards and stands. Her expression softens for a fleeting moment, the teasing smile becoming something almost affectionate.

"Until next time, Antonio."

And with that, she walks away, leaving you with a magnificent victory, a thoroughly ruined speech, and the uncomfortable suspicion that she enjoyed every second of it.

title: A Worthy Opponent

parameters.title: Competitive nature
parameters.description: Emma takes competition very seriously. She hates losing, but recognizes genuine skill in an opponent and is determined to learn from her mistakes.

variants.text: We met the first day right? Anyways.

text:
You find Emma studying a collection of cards, meticulously arranged across a table. She looks up as you approach.

"Antonio. To what do I owe the pleasure?"

You produce your latest creation, the _Happy Little Accident_, and place it before her.

"Another masterpiece, Fibonacci?" she asks, with a faint smile. "How fortunate that modesty isn't one of your weaknesses."

She picks up the card, apparently intending to give it a cursory inspection. Then she turns it toward the light. Her smile fades into concentration.

"Hmm."

She studies the card more closely, examining the intricate blue enchantments. For a moment, she seems to forget you're there.

"Interesting. Very interesting, actually."

She catches herself, sets the card down, and folds her hands.

"Well. It's certainly not terrible. How did you manage this?"

An excellent question. One you would very much like to know the answer to yourself.

parameters.text:
Emma looks from the card to you.

"You're giving it to me?"

For once, she seems genuinely surprised. She glances down at the card again.

"Antonio, this is an exceptional piece of work. You could win matches with it. Quite a few matches, in fact."

You assure her that you know perfectly well what you're offering.

She considers you for a moment, then carefully places the card among her own.

"Very well. I accept. But don't imagine this means I'll go easy on you in our next match."

A small smile appears.

"Especially now that you've been kind enough to improve my deck."

optionTemplates.text: "Would you like to know how I made it?"

parameters.text:
Emma's eyes return immediately to the card.

"I think I can work out the essentials myself, thank you."

She pauses.

"Although... that third enchantment is rather unconventional."

You explain the technique as best you can, carefully omitting certain details involving your elbow and a rather unfortunate jar of pigment. Emma listens intently, occasionally asking a question so precise that you find yourself reconsidering your own explanation.

Eventually, she leans back.

"That's clever. I wouldn't have approached it that way."

She takes a sheet of paper and begins sketching a variation.

"Of course, there's a way to improve it."

Naturally. You would have been disappointed otherwise.

optionTemplates.text: "Not bad, is it? Think you can do better?"

parameters.text:
Emma looks at you over the edge of the card.

"Oh, so that's why you're here."

She examines it once more, then returns it with exaggerated care.

"I admit, Antonio, you've set a rather interesting standard."

She gathers her books, a mischievous glint in her eyes.

"I was planning a quiet afternoon of study, but apparently I have something more important to do."

"What's that?"

She gives you a sweet smile.

"Improve upon your work, obviously."

title: Handmade Card

parameters.title: Unusual crafting techniques
parameters.description: Emma is fascinated by unusual crafting techniques and has a particular interest in blue magic.

title: The Ballet Incident
text:
You're enjoying a peaceful break in the cafeteria with Molly, Henry and Ousmane when Elsa bursts in, barely containing her laughter.

"You simply _must_ come and see this! It's hilarious! She thinks she's some sort of fairy!"

The four of you exchange puzzled looks.

"Emma, that insufferable little princess! Oh, just come along!"

Curiosity gets the better of you, and you follow Elsa through the Academy corridors to a small exercise hall.

Inside, Emma is practicing ballet alone. Dressed in a simple dance outfit, she stands beside a wooden barre, one hand resting lightly upon it. Her other hand holds her raised foot high above her head, at the end of a perfectly straight, almost impossibly vertical leg. Her balance is flawless, her expression one of absolute concentration. She hasn't noticed you.

Elsa turns toward the group, positively glowing with anticipation of the sarcastic remarks to come.

Instead, she finds Molly applauding very softly, her face alight with admiration, and three young men standing perfectly still, mouths hanging open, apparently hypnotized.

{{emmaSmittenReaction}}

Elsa's triumphant smile collapses.

"Oh, for heaven's sake! You're all _hopeless!_"

She storms off, her indignant footsteps echoing so loudly through the hall that Emma finally notices her audience.

Henry and Ousmane, caught red-handed, turn scarlet and beat a hasty retreat. Molly gives Emma a delighted smile and an enthusiastic thumbs-up before following them.

And suddenly, there's only you.

Emma calmly lowers her leg, turns toward you, and raises one eyebrow. A mischievous little smile plays at the corner of her mouth, as though she's daring you to say something.

variants.text: Honestly, this girl ought to be illegal. How on earth are you supposed to get any sleep tonight?

emmaSmittenReaction.fallback: You have to admit, it's quite a sight. You'd known Emma was talented, but apparently her determination to excel extends well beyond the card table.

parameters.title: Ballet
parameters.description: Emma is an accomplished ballet dancer, possessing remarkable grace, strength and flexibility.

parameters.text:
You incline your head appreciatively.

"I went to see the National Ballet back home last year. I must say, you wouldn't have looked out of place on that stage. Holding a pose like that with such grace isn't something one sees every day."

Emma's raised eyebrow slowly settles.

"Well, Fibonacci. I had no idea you were a patron of the fine arts."

A mischievous smile touches her lips.

"You really ought to invite our dear Baroness sometime. A little culture might do her a world of good."

She gives you a graceful little wave as she heads toward the changing rooms.

"Well, that wasn't quite the reaction Elsa was hoping for," you remark with a wink.

Emma relaxes at once, a broad, infectious smile spreading across her face.

"No, I believe she rolled a critical failure on that particular spell."

She glances toward the corridor, still smiling.

"All that effort to assemble an audience, too. Poor Elsa. One almost feels sorry for her."

"Almost?"

"Let's not get carried away, Antonio."

She gives you a conspiratorial wink before collecting her things.

"Emma, er... hello. I... very nice, yes. Very straight, and everything..."

Emma approaches with the delighted expression of a cat that has just discovered a particularly entertaining mouse.

"Ah, Antonio! My most devoted admirer! I see you're quite the ballet enthusiast. The tutus, the flexibility, the _physique_, above all. Am I right?"

Oh, dear.

"Er, yes. The physique. Exceptional, yes..."

Emma's smile grows positively wicked.

"Antonio, if we're going to be seeing each other in class all year, you'll really have to learn to resist certain enchantments."

She pauses, looking you straight in the eye.

"Otherwise, I'm afraid your grades are going to suffer terribly."

She walks away with a perfectly innocent expression, leaving you to contemplate the urgent need for remedial lessons in magical resistance.

You shrug, doing your best to look unimpressed.

"Not bad, Delamain. A little showy, perhaps."

Emma's eyebrow climbs a little higher.

"Showy?"

"Well, you certainly know how to make an entrance. Or rather, how to keep an audience."

Emma studies you for a moment. Then a slow smile spreads across her face.

title: An Unexpected Debt
text:
You encounter Emma in a quiet corridor of the Academy, standing by a window with a letter in her hands. She seems unusually still, her eyes fixed on the page. As you approach, she hastily folds the letter and slips it into her pocket. By the time she turns toward you, her familiar composure has almost returned.

"Antonio. What a pleasant surprise." Her smile is perfectly polite, and almost perfectly convincing.

You ask whether something is wrong.

"Nothing worth troubling you with." She looks away, then lets out a quiet sigh. "Oh, very well. It seems my bank has developed an exciting new interpretation of our agreement. One in which I owe them rather a lot of money, rather sooner than expected."

She attempts a dismissive smile, but it doesn't quite work. "I borrowed the money to pay my tuition. I've been working towards a place here for years, and I thought I had everything arranged." She pauses, looking through the window at the Academy grounds. "If I cannot meet their demand, I may have to leave."

For a moment, she seems very far away. Then she straightens her shoulders.

"Well. I've faced worse difficulties." Her voice regains some of its customary firmness. "I'll find a solution. I always do."

text:
Professor Glützenbaum enters the classroom with a letter in his hand and an expression suggesting that someone has committed a grave offense against civilization. He marches to his lectern, waits for silence, and adjusts his spectacles.

"Students. I have received an invitation from the Royal College of Artificery of Falkenstein. They are organizing a competition for first-year students, in which each participating Academy will send two representatives to demonstrate their talents in card crafting and tournament play."

A murmur of excitement runs through the room. Glützenbaum raises his hand.

"Allow me to read their invitation."

He clears his throat. "'It would give us the greatest pleasure to welcome representatives of your venerable institution, whose dedication to preserving the traditional methods of artificery is widely appreciated.'"

He pauses. His left eyebrow twitches.

"'While we recognize that certain provincial academies may lack access to the most recent advances in our discipline, we firmly believe that exposure to the standards of our leading institutions can only benefit their promising young scholars.'"

The room goes very quiet.

"'We therefore warmly encourage your participation, regardless of the eventual results, in the spirit of academic fellowship and mutual enrichment.'"

Glützenbaum lowers the letter.

"**Regardless of the eventual results.**"

He lets the words hang in the air.

"These pompous, silk-robed, overfunded—" He stops, straightens his spectacles, and takes a breath. "These esteemed colleagues appear to have forgotten that some of the finest artificers in the history of the discipline received their education within these very walls!"

The classroom erupts. Molly, usually so reserved, is on her feet, punching the air with both fists and cheering enthusiastically. Ousmane leans back in his chair, slowly twirling his magnificent moustache with the expression of a general contemplating a particularly satisfying campaign. Farid has produced a small knife and is flipping it expertly between his fingers, apparently considering the matter settled in favor of hostilities.

Someone at the back of the room shouts, "We'll show them!" Several others take up the cry. Glützenbaum makes a token attempt to restore order, but his heart is plainly not in it.

"Quite right!" he thunders, then remembers himself. "That is to say, we shall respond with the utmost dignity, professionalism, and devastating academic superiority!"

He strikes the lectern with his palm. A small cloud of chalk dust rises dramatically.

"Now! Each institution must appoint a captain, who will select a second student. I have given this matter considerable thought, and our captain shall be Miss Emma Delamain."

There is an enthusiastic round of applause. Emma rises gracefully from her seat, accepting the nomination with a composed smile that nevertheless betrays a certain fierce satisfaction.

"Thank you, Professor. I shall endeavor to make the Academy proud."

"I have every confidence that you will, Miss Delamain. And whom would you choose as your partner?"

"Antonio Fibonacci."

She answers without a moment's hesitation. You look up. A few heads turn in your direction.

Glützenbaum nods thoughtfully. "An interesting choice. Are you quite certain?"

"Entirely."

She turns toward you, her expression now wearing that familiar mixture of amusement and challenge.

"Unless, of course, Antonio has suddenly developed an objection to winning."

You have scarcely begun to formulate a response when Glützenbaum claps his hands.

"Excellent! Delamain and Fibonacci shall represent us. You have one week to prepare. I expect discipline, ingenuity, and above all, a performance that will make our distinguished colleagues regret having learned to write letters!"

The room bursts into applause once more. Ousmane rises to shake your hand with great solemnity. Molly beams at you from across the classroom. Farid gives you an approving nod and, mercifully, puts away his knife.

As the students begin to disperse, Emma approaches you with the purposeful stride of someone whose campaign has already begun.

"Tomorrow evening. My room. Bring your best deck, your crafting notes, and any ideas you consider worth defending. We have a great deal of work ahead of us."

"Do I get any say in this?"

"Certainly. You may choose whether to arrive at seven or disappoint me."

She gives you a wicked little smile.

"And Antonio? Do try to get some rest tonight. I intend to be extremely demanding."

With that, she sweeps out of the classroom, leaving you to contemplate the peculiar honor of having been recruited into Emma Delamain's personal war against the Royal College of Falkenstein.
title: The Challenge

text:
Emma's lodgings occupy a modest room on the upper floor of a rustic village inn. A narrow bed stands against one wall, a battered armchair occupies the other, and nearly every remaining surface has been conquered by books. A small kettle steams beside two cups on the desk. Apparently, your arrival has been anticipated with military precision.

"Seven o'clock. Excellent." Emma opens the door wider. "I was beginning to wonder whether I'd need to send a search party."

{{ greeting }}

She leads you to the desk, where two decks lie beside a rather alarming collection of tournament regulations, strategic diagrams, and handwritten notes. Evidently, Emma has not spent the afternoon idle.

"We have a few evenings before Falkenheim, and a great deal to accomplish. Unfortunately, time is a resource even I haven't yet learned to manufacture." She points to two piles of documents. "So we must choose our priorities."

"We could study our opponents, learn how they play, and prepare something unpleasant for them. Or we could concentrate on our own performance and spend tonight practicing against each other."

She smiles, with the dangerous enthusiasm of someone who considers both possibilities excellent entertainment.

"Well, partner? How shall we spend our evening?"

parameters.text:
"If we know how they play, we can prepare a counter-strategy. Why fight them on their terms?"

"An excellent principle." Emma considers the tournament invitation again. "And I believe I know where we might begin."

Her expression brightens with a rather mischievous idea.

"Elsa Falkenstein."

"We know our own decks better than theirs. Let's put that advantage to work. A few practice games should reveal where we need improvement."

"Splendid." Emma pushes the documents aside and begins arranging her cards.

"Although I must warn you, Antonio, I have no intention of going easy on you merely because we're on the same team."

You wouldn't dream of asking.

"He's almost certainly their captain. And Elsa knows him rather well, as siblings unfortunately tend to."

"Then we should ask her."

"Yes." Emma purses her lips. "There's just one small complication."

She reminds you of that unfortunate incident at the ballet, when Elsa attempted to make a spectacle of her and ended up providing the entertainment herself.

"I doubt she's forgiven me. Which is rather unfair, since I wasn't the one who arranged the whole thing."

A short walk brings you to Elsa's lodgings, in an inn whose polished marble entrance and liveried servants suggest an establishment considerably more prosperous than Emma's. Elsa receives you in a beautifully furnished sitting room, where she listens to your explanation with growing amusement.

"So. The illustrious Emma Delamain has come to ask for _my_ assistance."

"Information, Elsa. Not divine intervention."

"How disappointing. I was rather looking forward to the latter."

Elsa settles into her upholstered chair, crossing one leg elegantly over the other.

"My brother is an exceptional player. I know his preferred cards, his strategies, even his latest decklist." She smiles. "But why, exactly, should I share any of that with you?"

parameters.text:
"Elsa, surely you'd rather see your own Academy win than have Falkenheim boast about humiliating it. Imagine having to listen to your brother recount his triumph every time you visit home."

Elsa's expression changes.

"Of course I would." Elsa smiles pleasantly. "And I shall be cheering for you with tremendous enthusiasm."

"And the information?"

"Oh, I couldn't possibly betray my dear brother's confidence. Family loyalty, you understand."

Emma's jaw tightens. For a moment, you think she's about to deliver a reply that will end the conversation rather spectacularly.

Instead, she takes a breath.

"Very well, Elsa. What would you want in exchange?"

Elsa sits up, suddenly interested.

"Oh?"

"A favor. From both of us. Something reasonable, to be agreed upon when you need it."

Elsa studies the two of you in delighted silence. Her gaze travels from Emma to you and back again, as though assessing a pair of newly acquired servants.

"How _interesting_." She taps a finger against her lips. "The brilliant Emma Delamain and her promising young associate, both at my disposal. I must say, the possibilities are rather intoxicating."

"Within reason," Emma repeats firmly.

"Naturally, darling. I would never dream of asking anything unreasonable."

Something about the way she says this makes you profoundly uneasy.

Elsa retrieves a folded decklist from her desk and hands it to Emma.

"There you are. Now, I shall have to think very carefully about what to ask of you."

As you leave the inn, you turn to Emma.

"Are you sure this was a good idea? What do you think she's going to want?"

"I haven't the faintest idea."

"That doesn't worry you?"

"Not particularly. We've obtained what we came for."

She unfolds the decklist and begins studying it as she walks.

"Honestly, Antonio, do try to concentrate on the important things."

"Your brother must be an excellent strategist," you remark. "I imagine he's already prepared something to counter our Academy's usual defensive decks."

Elsa gives a dismissive little laugh.

"Defensive decks? Please. He'd overwhelm those before they could establish themselves. His sacrificial combinations are quite impossible to—"

She stops.

You smile.

Emma's expression becomes one of profound appreciation.

"Elsa," she says gently, "I believe Antonio was asking a question."

Elsa stares at you both.

"I despise clever people."

"An unfortunate prejudice," Emma replies, "particularly at an Academy."

You continue the conversation, carefully encouraging Elsa to correct your increasingly inaccurate guesses about her brother's strategy. Eventually, exasperated by your apparent ignorance, she snatches a sheet of paper from her desk.

"Oh, for heaven's sake. Here! This is his decklist. Perhaps you'll understand what I'm talking about when you see it."

Emma accepts the document with a gracious smile.

"How very instructive. Thank you, Elsa."

It is only as you rise to leave that Elsa seems to reconsider the entire conversation.

"Wait a moment..."

You begin probing Elsa's knowledge with what you consider a series of subtle questions.

Unfortunately, Elsa proves rather less susceptible to subtlety than you'd hoped.

"Antonio, darling, if you want to know my brother's strategy, you could simply ask." She smiles. "I would still refuse, naturally, but we'd save ourselves so much time."

Emma hides a smile behind her hand.

"An admirable attempt, Fibonacci. Perhaps we should try a less elaborate approach."

She turns to Elsa, her expression becoming unusually serious.

"All right. What would it take for you to give us that decklist?"

Elsa arches an eyebrow.

"Are you offering to beg?"

"Don't be absurd. I'm offering you a favor. From both of us, whenever you might need it."

You turn toward Emma, rather alarmed by the sudden generosity of this proposal.

Elsa, meanwhile, looks as though someone has just presented her with a particularly magnificent birthday gift.

"Both of you?" She studies you in turn, her smile widening. "My dear Emma, I had no idea you could be so accommodating."

"Do you accept or not?"

"Oh, absolutely."

She opens a drawer, retrieves a folded sheet, and hands it to Emma with considerable ceremony.

"One complete decklist, as requested. And two exceptionally talented Academy students owing me a favor. What a delightful afternoon."

On the way back, you finally manage to interrupt Emma's enthusiastic examination of the document.

"Emma. About that favor..."

"Yes?"

"We have absolutely no idea what Elsa is going to ask us to do."

"No."

"And you don't find that concerning?"

Emma looks up at you, apparently surprised.

"Antonio, we have the decklist. We can worry about everything else after we've won."

You are beginning to suspect that Emma Delamain's attitude toward risk depends rather heavily on whether she considers the objective sufficiently glorious.

"Can you believe them? All airs and graces until someone gives them a proper thrashing, and then their true colors come out! Miserable scoundrels! Blackguards! Unspeakable little weasels!"

"Ah."

You and Emma stare into the back of the cart.

It is packed to the brim with vegetables. There is barely room for two people, let alone two people and a trophy the size of a small child. Emma, who has been gazing at the latter with undisguised affection ever since the award ceremony, suddenly seems rather less enamored of it.

"Would you prefer to sit on the carrots or the potatoes, darling?"

"Oh, give it a rest. He can't hear you anymore."

"I know, my love."

Emma rolls her eyes and climbs aboard.

To your surprise, she reveals a remarkable talent for logistics. Within moments, a few crates have been shifted, several sacks rearranged, and a small, reasonably comfortable nest has emerged between a wall of cabbages and a heap of apples.

She settles into it, draws her knees up, and pats the floor beside her.

The smile on her face suggests that revenge is imminent.

"Don't be shy, sweetheart."

Oh, no.

Forty centimeters. At most.

You swallow and sit down as far from her as physically possible, which turns out to mean pressed firmly against her side, with the enormous trophy balanced across your knees.

"Not going to faint on me, are you, Fibonacci?"

You brace yourself for several hours of merciless teasing.

But, unexpectedly, Emma merely gives you a peaceful little smile. The cart lurches forward, and she turns to watch the countryside roll past.

No sarcastic remarks. No clever observations at your expense.

Well.

Here you are, then.

Lovely weather, isn't it?

And, er...

Oh, for heaven's sake, _say something._

You risk a glance at Emma. She's watching the distant hills, looking almost dreamy. Several minutes pass. She doesn't appear troubled by the silence in the slightest.

Then she turns toward you.

Quick. Think of something.

But she only smiles, very slightly, before looking away again.

Eventually, she takes a book from her bag and begins reading. Every now and then, she comes across a passage she particularly enjoys and reads it aloud to you, supplying a scholarly commentary that is considerably longer than the passage itself.

Naturally, this also presents opportunities to remind you that a little more reading would do you a world of good.

The hours slip by. The afternoon light softens. The sun sinks toward the horizon.

After the madness of the past week, exhaustion begins to catch up with you.

You really ought to stay awake. It would be terribly embarrassing to—

When you open your eyes again, it is dark.

Someone has tucked a blanket around you.

That's... rather nice, actually.

Wait.

Something isn't quite right.

Your head.

Oh.

{{shoulderRealization}}

Very slowly, you lift it. Straighten your back. Fix your eyes on the darkness ahead.

Whatever you do, don't look at her.

The cart rattles to a stop.

"Sleep well?"

Emma is pressing her lips together, plainly struggling not to laugh.

Mercifully, she says nothing more.

"Come on. We're here."

Being summoned to the administrator's office first thing in the morning is rarely a cause for celebration. You and Emma arrive with matching expressions of suspicion, although Emma has at least made an effort to look respectable.

The administrator, however, seems positively delighted.

"Ah! Our champions! Come in, come in!" He gestures toward the chairs opposite his desk. "I have some excellent news. The Academy's reputation has benefited enormously from your little expedition to Falkenheim. The Board of Governors is most pleased."

Emma exchanges a glance with you. You've never heard the words _Board of Governors_ and _pleased_ in the same sentence before.

"Ordinarily, your tournament prize would take several weeks to process. However, in recognition of the prestige you've brought us, the Academy has decided to advance the reward from its own treasury."

"In actual money?"
