"Cash," she says immediately.

"Perhaps you'd like to consider—"

"Cash."

"Very well, then."

He makes a note, carefully avoiding your eyes.

"And there is one more thing."

From a drawer, he produces two cards and places them on the desk.

You recognize the imposing towers, elegant courtyards, and familiar spires of your own Academy. Beautifully rendered, the illustration seems almost alive with magical energy.

"A commemorative Academy land card, for each of you. Commissioned especially for our victorious representatives."

Emma picks hers up with almost reverent care.

"A land card?" She examines it from several angles. "But these are advanced enchantments! We won't even begin studying their construction until our later years."

"Quite so. Consider it an investment in the Academy's future champions."

Emma is too busy admiring her card to notice the administrator looking rather pleased with that last remark.

"And you, Mr. Fibonacci? Which reward would you prefer?"

parameters.text:
"I'll take the money, thank you."

"A sound decision," Emma says with obvious approval.

The administrator counts out your reward and presents you with a receipt requiring only three signatures.

You sign the first.

Then the second.

By the third, you begin to understand why the Academy employs so many administrators.

"I'll take the discount at the materials shop."

Emma raises an eyebrow.

"An interesting choice, Fibonacci."

"Think how much we spend on crafting materials."

"Oh, I've thought about it. Extensively." She glances at her own reward. "But I rather suspect my banker would be less enthusiastic about accepting discounted gemstones in lieu of payment."

The administrator hands you a stamped certificate.

"Twenty percent off, valid for one year. Non-transferable, non-refundable, and subject to the usual conditions."

"How many conditions?"

"Only forty-seven."

Emma looks at you with profound sympathy.

title: The Spoils of Victory

parameters.title: Financial independence
parameters.description: Her tournament prize has allowed her to repay her tuition loan, removing the immediate threat to her education.

afterPrize.text:
Outside the office, Emma stops in the corridor and looks down at the purse in her hand.

Then she laughs.

Not her usual little sarcastic laugh, either. A genuine, delighted laugh that makes a passing student turn to stare.

"Antonio. I'm going to pay it off."

"Your loan?"

"Every last coin. The bank, the interest, those dreadful letters..." She gives the purse a little shake. "All of it. Gone!"

She looks almost dizzy with relief.

"I've spent months calculating how much I owe, how much I can earn, how long I can possibly stay here. And now..."

For a moment, she seems unable to finish the sentence.

Then she looks up at you, grinning.

"I can actually afford to be a student!"

"An alarming prospect. You might have time to enjoy yourself."

"Don't be ridiculous, Fibonacci. I have far too much work to—"

She stops.

A thoughtful expression crosses her face.

"Well. Perhaps a _little_ time."

{{tutoringThanks}}

variants.text:
"And you know, with the money I'm earning from Molly's tutoring project, I might even be able to afford a few luxuries now and then."

She says the word _luxuries_ with the cautious fascination of someone discussing a rare and potentially dangerous magical substance.

Then her expression softens.

"Speaking of which, Antonio..."

She reaches over and gives your arm a brief, affectionate squeeze.

"Thank you. For suggesting me to Molly, I mean. I don't think I ever properly thanked you for that."

"You did, actually."

"Well, I'm doing it again. Try to endure the experience."

Her smile widens.

"Come on. I'm buying you a coffee at the cafeteria."

"You're buying?"

"Yes, Fibonacci. With my own money. A truly historic occasion."

She starts down the corridor, then looks back.

"And don't get carried away. One coffee. I'm not made of money."

tutoringThanks.fallback:
She slips the purse safely into her bag, still smiling to herself.

"Well, I ought to visit the bank before my next class."

"Already?"

"Antonio, I've been dreaming of that moment for months. I'm not waiting another day."

She takes a few steps, then turns back.

"And we should celebrate properly sometime. Preferably somewhere that doesn't charge extra for a clean table."

She gives you a bright smile.

"See you later, Fibonacci!"

text:
You arrive at the artificery classroom a little early and find Emma already at her desk, reading a letter. She looks unusually pleased with herself.

"Antonio! Excellent. I was hoping to catch you before class."

She folds the letter and sets it aside.

"Have you heard about the Academy's annual ball next Saturday? Apparently, it's quite the occasion. Music, dancing, extravagant dresses, and enough distinguished guests to populate a royal court."

You have heard something about it.

"Well, I have a particular interest in one of those guests. Lord de Varenne. An elderly gentleman, enormously respected, and one of the greatest patrons of artificery in the kingdom. He's helped launch the careers of several remarkable scholars."

Her green eyes brighten with unmistakable ambition.

"An introduction could open some very interesting doors. And I intend to make a good impression."

She pauses, then gives you a mischievous smile.

"Naturally, a young lady cannot attend such an occasion without a suitable escort. And I believe I know just the gentleman."

You look around the classroom, wondering whom she has in mind.

"Don't be obtuse, Fibonacci. I'm inviting _you_."

{{ ballet_recollection }}

"So, Antonio. Would you do me the honor of accompanying me to the ball? I promise excellent company, a respectable amount of dancing, and only a modest risk of social humiliation."

She considers that last promise.

"Well. I promise to do my best."

parameters.text:
"An evening of excellent food, dancing, and the most promising artificer of our generation? How could I refuse?"

Emma beams.

"Splendid! I knew you'd recognize a good opportunity when one presented itself."

She retrieves a small notebook and makes a mark beside something she's already written.

"You've put me on a list?"

"Naturally. One must plan ahead."

She studies you for a moment, her expression growing thoughtful.

"Although there is one small matter we'll need to address."

"What matter?"

"Your wardrobe."

You glance down at your clothes.

"What's wrong with my wardrobe?"

"Nothing at all. For attending lectures, visiting the library, or digging potatoes."

She gives you a reassuring pat on the arm.

"Don't worry, Antonio. I'll take care of everything. Meet me in town tomorrow afternoon. We'll find you something suitable."

The professor enters, and Emma turns toward the front of the classroom with a perfectly innocent expression.

You have the distinct impression that you've just volunteered for considerably more than an evening of dancing.

"I'm flattered, Emma. Truly. But I think I'll have to decline."

For a moment, she looks surprised. Then she gives a small, accepting nod.

"Of course. A pity, but I understand."

She picks up her letter again, tapping it thoughtfully against the desk.

"Well, I'll simply have to make other arrangements. It would be absurd to miss such an opportunity for want of a dancing partner."

Her familiar smile returns.

"And frankly, I was being rather generous in overlooking your questionable qualifications."

"Questionable?"

"Entirely unproven on the dance floor, Fibonacci. A considerable risk."

You laugh, and she gives you a friendly little wave as the professor enters.

"Enjoy your Saturday evening, Antonio. I shall endeavor to become rich and famous in your absence."

title: An Invitation of Sorts

parameters.title: Professional ambition
parameters.description: Emma hopes to meet Lord de Varenne at the Academy ball. He is a distinguished patron of artificery whose support could greatly advance her career.

variants.text:
She rests her chin on one hand, looking thoroughly entertained.

"After all, I remember how deeply you appreciated my ballet performance. Such an extraordinary connoisseur of the fine arts."

She pauses delicately.

"Particularly the _physique_, if memory serves. And I assure you, Antonio, I intend to look absolutely spectacular."

Her smile becomes positively wicked.

"Though you will be expected to remain capable of speech this time. We shall be in distinguished company."

"Besides, I happen to know that you're a great admirer of dancing. I remember that expression on your face when Elsa so kindly arranged our little demonstration."

She looks at you with innocent curiosity.

"Was it my technique that impressed you, I wonder? My balance? My artistic interpretation?"

Her lips twitch.

"Or were you simply overwhelmed by the beauty of classical ballet?"

"And since you were so gracious about my dancing last time, I thought you might appreciate another opportunity to judge my performance."

She raises an eyebrow.

"I believe your exact words were _a little showy_. Well, Fibonacci, I intend to be positively magnificent. Try not to look too impressed."

ballet_recollection.fallback:
"And you've already seen me dance, of course. Under rather unusual circumstances, admittedly."

She smiles at the memory.

"Poor Elsa. All that trouble to arrange an audience, only to discover that everyone rather enjoyed the performance."

She gives a little shrug.

"I thought this time we might attend somewhere we're actually invited."

title: A Question of Elegance
text:
The shop Emma has chosen stands on one of the more fashionable streets of the town, its windows displaying embroidered waistcoats, elegant coats, and garments whose prices appear to have been calculated by someone with a personal grudge against students.

Emma is waiting outside, looking entirely at ease.

"Antonio! Right on time. Come along, we have work to do."

Inside, a dignified tailor greets you with a polite bow. His enthusiasm increases noticeably when Emma begins examining his finest merchandise.

"Something suitable for the Academy ball," she explains. "Elegant, distinguished, but not excessively ostentatious. We want to make a good impression, not declare war on the aristocracy."

The tailor nods gravely and disappears among the shelves.

What follows is a rather exhausting series of fittings.

The first coat makes you look, according to Emma, "like a provincial tax collector attending his own funeral." The second is apparently designed for a man of considerably greater girth. A third features so much embroidery that Emma takes one look at you and bursts into laughter.

"Oh, Antonio. You look like a prince!"

"Excellent."

"A prince who has misplaced both his kingdom and his judgment. Take it off."

Eventually, after considerable discussion, the tailor produces three outfits that meet Emma's exacting standards.

The first is a handsome, understated ensemble in dark wool, well cut and entirely respectable. The second is considerably finer, with rich fabrics, careful embroidery, and the unmistakable appearance of a gentleman accustomed to good company. The third is a particularly striking creation of deep blue velvet and silver detailing, elegant enough to attract attention without quite becoming ridiculous.

Emma studies all three with the concentration of someone evaluating competing designs for an exceptionally important enchantment.

"Well, Fibonacci. They all have their merits. The first is perfectly respectable, the second is rather distinguished, and the third..."

She considers the elaborate blue coat.

"The third would certainly make an impression."

Then she turns toward you with a mischievous smile.

"So. How much of your fortune are you prepared to sacrifice upon the altar of elegance?"

parameters.text:
You settle on the modest dark wool ensemble. The tailor makes a few adjustments, and you examine yourself in the mirror with considerable satisfaction.

"Perfectly respectable," Emma declares, walking slowly around you. "A sensible choice. Understated, practical, and quite flattering."

"High praise indeed."

"Don't become accustomed to it."

She straightens your collar and steps back.

"There. You look like a young gentleman with excellent prospects and the good sense not to spend them all on clothing."

"Almost as though I belong among the aristocracy."

"Oh, let's not be ambitious, Antonio. We can manage _well-dressed_. Aristocratic manners may take a little longer."

She smiles, clearly pleased with the result.

parameters.name: Respectable Evening Attire
parameters.description: A well-tailored ensemble of dark wool, with a crisp linen shirt and a modest embroidered waistcoat. Understated, practical, and entirely suitable for respectable company.

parameters.text:
You choose the distinguished ensemble. The tailor helps you into the fine coat, adjusts its embroidered cuffs, and presents you before the mirror.

Emma studies you with evident approval.

"Now _that_ is considerably better."

She approaches, brushes an imaginary speck of dust from your shoulder, and adjusts the fold of your cravat.

"Stand straight, Antonio."

You oblige.

"Chin up. Shoulders back."

"Anything else, Your Majesty?"

"Yes. Try not to speak until I've finished admiring my work."

She takes a step back, tilts her head, and smiles.

"Actually... yes. That suits you rather well."

For a moment, she seems genuinely impressed. Then her familiar composure returns.

"Remarkable what proper tailoring can accomplish."

You decide to accept the compliment before she has time to qualify it further.

parameters.name: Distinguished Evening Suit
parameters.description: An elegant formal ensemble of fine charcoal wool, with tasteful embroidery, polished buttons, and a beautifully tailored waistcoat. The attire of a confident young gentleman who knows how to present himself in distinguished company.

parameters.text:
You point toward the elaborate blue velvet ensemble.

"That one."

Emma's eyebrows rise.

"Antonio. Are you quite certain?"

"Absolutely. You said we ought to make an impression."

"I did. I wasn't necessarily suggesting we attempt to outshine the entire nobility."

Nevertheless, she looks delighted as the tailor helps you into the magnificent coat.

The fabric is extraordinarily fine, the silver embroidery delicate and intricate. When the tailor finishes, Emma falls silent.

She looks you up and down, her expression unusually difficult to read.

"Well?" you ask.

"One moment."

She circles you slowly, examining the cut of the shoulders, the fall of the fabric, the silver clasp at your throat.

Then she smiles.

"Oh, Antonio. That is _splendid_."

"Really?"

"Quite. In fact, I'm beginning to worry that I've created a rival for the attention of every lady at the ball."

"Should I be concerned?"

"Not at all. I shall simply inform them that you're terribly dull and have no prospects whatsoever."

She gives you a brilliant smile.

"Come along, Your Highness. Before I change my mind and insist on something less magnificent."

parameters.name: Magnificent Blue Velvet Attire
parameters.description: A sumptuous formal ensemble of deep blue velvet, richly decorated with exquisite silver embroidery and a matching waistcoat. Striking, elegant, and unmistakably expensive. A garment designed to draw admiring glances in the grandest of ballrooms.

a_finishing_touch.text:
With your new clothes carefully wrapped, you prepare to leave the shop. Emma, however, suddenly remembers something.

"Oh! One moment, Antonio. I nearly forgot."

She turns back toward the tailor and exchanges a few quiet words with him. You wait near the door while he retrieves a small box from behind the counter.

A little later, Emma emerges looking suspiciously pleased with herself.

"Here."

She presses the box into your hands.

Inside is a beautifully crafted silver cravat pin, its head decorated with a small, deep blue gemstone.

"Emma, what's this?"

"A finishing touch, obviously. You can hardly attend the Academy ball with an improperly secured cravat."

"You bought this for me?"

"Well, I certainly didn't buy it for myself. I have no intention of wearing a cravat."

You examine the little pin. It's an elegant piece, and judging by the craftsmanship, not an inexpensive one.

"Emma, you really didn't have to."

"I know."

Her answer is unusually simple. She watches you for a moment, then gives a small smile.

"Consider it a thank-you for agreeing to accompany me. And for putting up with an entire afternoon of my excellent advice."

She pauses.

"Besides, I thought the blue would suit you."

For a moment, the usual teasing is absent from her expression.

Then she recovers.

"Now, do put it away before you lose it. I'd hate to discover that my investment in your appearance was entirely wasted."

parameters.text:
"Thank you, Emma. It's a beautiful gift."

Her expression softens.

"You're very welcome, Antonio."

She takes your arm as you leave the shop, looking rather pleased with the afternoon's accomplishments.

"Well. One problem solved. Now all we need is for you to remember which foot goes where on the dance floor."

"You're not worried?"

"Not particularly. I happen to be an excellent dancer."

You suspect Saturday evening is going to be quite an experience.

parameters.name: Emma's Silver Cravat Pin
parameters.description: An elegant silver cravat pin set with a small deep blue gemstone, given to Antonio by Emma during their preparations for the Academy ball. A thoughtful gift from a friend with impeccable taste.

parameters.text:
"A present, Delamain? Why, I'm touched. One might almost think you're fond of me."

Emma gives you a patient look.

"Don't be absurd, Fibonacci. I simply refuse to be seen in public with a gentleman whose accessories offend my sense of aesthetics."

"So it's purely a matter of professional necessity?"

"Entirely."

You turn the little pin over in your hand.

"A very generous professional necessity."

She raises an eyebrow.

"Would you prefer I take it back?"

"Absolutely not."

"Then I suggest you stop interrogating your benefactor."

She slips her arm through yours and leads you toward the door.

"Come along. We have a ball to attend, and I have a reputation to maintain."

parameters.name: Emma's Silver Cravat Pin
parameters.description: An elegant silver cravat pin set with a small deep blue gemstone, given to Antonio by Emma during their preparations for the Academy ball. A thoughtful gift from a friend with impeccable taste.

a_finishing_touch.title: A Finishing Touch

title: The Best-Laid Plans
text:
The Academy's grand ballroom is a magnificent sight. Hundreds of candles illuminate the vaulted ceiling, their light reflected in towering mirrors and polished marble. Musicians perform from an elevated gallery, while elegantly dressed guests mingle beneath chandeliers that probably cost more than your entire education.

You adjust your collar, check that Emma's silver cravat pin is properly secured, and survey the gathering.

{{ outfit_reaction }}

You've barely finished admiring the surroundings when a familiar voice calls from behind you.

"Antonio!"

You turn.

And for a moment, you forget what you were going to say.

Emma stands at the entrance to the ballroom, wearing a breathtaking gown of deep emerald silk. The elegant cut accentuates her tall, graceful figure, while delicate silver embroidery catches the candlelight whenever she moves. Her long, wavy hair falls loosely over one shoulder, and a pair of familiar green gemstones glitters at her ears.

She looks absolutely stunning.

{{ emma_entrance }}

Emma approaches, clearly delighted by the effect of her entrance.

"Well, Fibonacci? Shall we?"

She offers you her hand.

"After all, we didn't spend an entire afternoon turning you into a gentleman merely to have you stand about admiring the architecture."

variants.text: Your magnificent blue velvet attire has already attracted several admiring glances. One elderly lady even mistakes you for the son of a visiting count, a misunderstanding you are in no particular hurry to correct.

Your finely tailored evening suit has proved an excellent investment. You look every inch a respectable young gentleman, and for once, nobody seems inclined to question your presence among such distinguished company.

outfit_reaction.fallback: Your new clothes fit comfortably and look perfectly respectable. Some of the guests are considerably more extravagantly dressed, but you suspect a few of them have spent the equivalent of a small house on their appearance.

variants.text:
"Oh, Emma. You look... I mean, that dress is... Good heavens."

A splendid speech. Truly worthy of the occasion.

Emma's smile widens. She steps closer, apparently taking considerable pleasure in your predicament.

"Antonio, darling, do try to remember how to breathe."

She turns gracefully, letting the silk of her gown flow around her.

"Well? I take it you approve?"

"Emma, you're magnificent."

This time, the words emerge without hesitation. She looks at you, and her teasing expression softens into something unexpectedly warm.

"Thank you, Antonio. That's very sweet."

For a moment, she seems almost shy. Then she gives you a mischievous smile.

"And here I was, beginning to worry that you'd developed an immunity to my charms. How reassuring to discover that your appreciation of _physique_ remains undiminished."

emma_entrance.fallback:
"Emma! You look wonderful."

She smiles, visibly pleased.

"Thank you, Antonio. You look rather splendid yourself."

She gives your outfit an approving glance.

"I must say, my efforts at the tailor's have been amply rewarded."

"You mean _my_ efforts. I was the one who had to endure the fittings."

"An indispensable contribution, certainly. Standing still is an art, and you've made remarkable progress."

parameters.title: A taste for elegance
parameters.description: Emma enjoys dancing, beautiful clothes, and sophisticated company, although she usually considers such pleasures secondary to her professional ambitions.

optionTemplates.text: Join Emma on the dance floor

parameters.text:
You take her hand and lead her toward the dancers.

Emma smiles.

"Excellent. And do remember, Antonio, the object is to move _with_ your partner, not to defeat her."

"That wasn't my intention."

"Good. I find competitive dancing terribly exhausting."

the_dance.text:
The orchestra begins a graceful waltz, and Emma moves effortlessly into your arms.

Dancing with her is a rather different experience from watching her practice ballet. She moves with such natural elegance that the steps seem almost to arrange themselves around her. When you hesitate, a subtle pressure from her hand or a barely perceptible shift of her weight guides you back into rhythm.

"Very good, Antonio," she murmurs. "You're doing splendidly."

"Surprised?"

"A little. I had prepared several encouraging remarks about perseverance and the dignity of failure."

"How disappointing for you."

"Devastating."

She laughs, and the two of you continue dancing.

One waltz becomes another. Between dances, you sample the excellent refreshments, exchange observations about the more extravagant guests, and occasionally find yourselves struggling to conceal your amusement at the elaborate rituals of polite society.

At one point, a particularly pompous gentleman delivers a lengthy speech about the declining standards of modern artificery, apparently unaware that Emma has published work contradicting nearly everything he says.

She listens with perfect courtesy.

"How fascinating," she tells him afterward. "I had no idea the field had advanced so little since your retirement."

You are forced to hide your laughter behind a glass of sparkling wine.

By the time the musicians pause for an interval, you've spent a remarkably enjoyable evening together.

Emma looks positively radiant.

Then, quite suddenly, she remembers something.

"Oh! Good heavens, Antonio. Lord de Varenne!"

She searches the room with renewed purpose.

"I've been having such a wonderful time that I'd almost forgotten why I came!"

She catches sight of a familiar heraldic emblem near the far end of the ballroom.

"There! Come along. I believe that's his family crest."

parameters.text:
You offer Emma your arm, and together you make your way through the crowded ballroom.

"Ready to conquer another corner of the civilized world, Delamain?"

"Naturally."

She gives you a determined smile.

"Although I do hope this conquest involves fewer casualties than our last tournament."

the_dance.title: An Excellent Evening

the_patron.text:
The gentleman standing beneath the de Varenne family crest is not remotely as old as Emma expected.

In fact, he appears scarcely older than thirty.

Tall, impeccably dressed, and possessed of the easy confidence of someone who has never had to worry about the cost of an evening's entertainment, he is speaking with a small group of Academy professors.

Emma hesitates.

"That's... not Lord de Varenne."

The gentleman notices your approach and offers a courteous smile.

"Good evening. May I help you?"

Emma recovers immediately.

"Forgive the interruption. I am Emma Delamain, a first-year student of artificery. I had hoped to meet Lord de Varenne this evening."

"Ah! My father, I presume?"

He smiles.

"I'm afraid he has decided that Academy balls are better suited to people whose knees still function properly. He sent me in his place."

He offers a slight bow.

"Lucien de Varenne. A pleasure, Mademoiselle Delamain."

Emma introduces you as well, and Lucien greets you with equal courtesy.

"Delamain..." he repeats thoughtfully. "Now, where have I heard that name?"

His expression brightens.

"Of course! The Falkenheim tournament. You represented the Academy, didn't you?"

Emma smiles.

"Indeed I did."

"Excellent! I've heard rather interesting things about your work. My father still takes a great interest in promising young artificers, and I've recently begun assisting him with some of his research initiatives."

He proceeds to ask Emma several surprisingly perceptive questions about her studies, her preferred branches of magic, and her ambitions after graduation.

Within minutes, they are discussing advanced enchantment techniques with such enthusiasm that you begin to wonder whether either remembers the orchestra is playing.

Lucien is clearly impressed.

And not, you notice, entirely by her scholarship.

His compliments are impeccably polite, but he seems particularly attentive to Emma's smile, and he finds a remarkable number of excuses to address her directly.

{{ patron_reaction }}

Then Lucien's expression grows more serious.

"Mademoiselle Delamain, I wonder whether you might be interested in a rather unusual opportunity."

variants.text:
You watch Lucien smile at Emma, and Emma smile politely in return.

Well. This is unfortunate.

He is handsome, wealthy, charming, impeccably connected, and apparently capable of discussing advanced artificery without sounding like an idiot.

You begin to suspect the universe has developed a personal interest in making your life difficult.

patron_reaction.fallback:
Lucien certainly seems to have taken an interest in Emma, and not exclusively in her scholarly accomplishments. You wonder whether she has noticed.

Knowing Emma, she probably has.

The more interesting question is what she intends to do about it.

parameters.text:
Emma leans forward slightly, her eyes bright with curiosity.

"An opportunity, Monsieur de Varenne? I'm listening."

Lucien smiles.

"I rather hoped you would be."

the_patron.title: A Distinguished Gentleman

the_offer.text:
"My family sponsors a number of research initiatives," Lucien explains. "One of them involves a small group of senior artificers working on advanced magical synthesis. Exceptional scholars, every one of them. They're currently looking for a promising younger collaborator."

Emma's expression changes at once.

"Which artificers?"

Lucien names three renowned masters of the discipline.

Emma stares at him.

"Professor Armand? _The_ Professor Armand?"

"The very same."

For a moment, she looks as though someone has just offered her the keys to the Royal Library.

Then she regains her composure.

"That's an extraordinary opportunity. But surely such a project would require a considerable commitment?"

"Indeed. It would involve regular correspondence, occasional travel, and a substantial amount of independent research. The compensation is modest, I'm afraid, but the experience would be invaluable. And my father has always been generous with recommendations for those who distinguish themselves."

Emma considers this carefully.

Lucien continues.

"Naturally, I would be delighted to discuss the arrangements in greater detail. Perhaps you might visit our residence sometime? I could show you the family's collection, and we might continue our conversation over dinner."

He smiles warmly.

"I confess, Mademoiselle Delamain, that I would find your company most agreeable."

Emma returns his smile with perfect courtesy, although you notice that she doesn't immediately accept the invitation.

"That is very kind of you, Monsieur de Varenne. Might I have a moment to consider?"

"Of course. Take all the time you need."

She draws you aside, just beyond earshot.

"Well, Antonio. This is rather unexpected."

Her excitement is unmistakable.

"Working with Armand and his colleagues! Can you imagine? I could learn more in a few months than most students manage in years."

Then her expression grows thoughtful.

"Although it would consume an enormous amount of time. And the compensation is hardly enough to justify neglecting my studies."

She glances back toward Lucien.

"He's certainly charming, isn't he?"

You make a noncommittal sound.

Emma gives you a sidelong look, but mercifully refrains from commenting.

"Anyway. You're the one person here whose judgment I trust. What do you think? Should I accept, or try to negotiate something else?"

parameters.text:
"Emma, this is exactly the sort of opportunity you've been working toward. Learning directly from people like Armand? You'd be mad to pass it up."

She considers your words, then slowly smiles.

"Yes. You're right."

"Of course I am."

"Do try not to ruin the moment, Antonio."

She laughs, then turns back toward Lucien.

"Monsieur de Varenne, I've considered your proposal. I would be delighted to participate."

"Wonderful!"

Lucien looks genuinely pleased.

"I shall arrange the introductions immediately. I believe you'll find the work fascinating."

Emma thanks him warmly. When he excuses himself to speak with another guest, she turns toward you, her eyes shining.

"Antonio. Professor Armand! I can hardly believe it."

"I noticed."

She catches your arm and gives it an excited squeeze.

"Oh, this could be extraordinary. Just think of everything I might learn!"

For once, her usual composure has given way entirely to enthusiasm.

You can't help smiling.

"It's an extraordinary offer, Emma. But you're already doing remarkably well at the Academy. Wouldn't it be better to concentrate on your studies for now?"

She frowns thoughtfully.

"Perhaps. Although the opportunity to work with Armand..."

"Could come again. Especially if you continue distinguishing yourself here."

Emma considers this for a moment.

Then her eyes brighten.

"Actually... I may have an idea."

She turns toward Lucien.

"Monsieur de Varenne, your proposal is extremely generous. Unfortunately, my academic commitments would make a long-term collaboration rather difficult at present."

Lucien looks disappointed.

"A pity. I had hoped—"

"However," Emma continues smoothly, "I wonder whether your family might be interested in commissioning a smaller piece of work?"

She explains that she has been experimenting with several promising enchantment techniques, but that certain rare ingredients remain prohibitively expensive. With the appropriate materials, she believes she could produce something quite exceptional.

Lucien listens with growing interest.

"A commissioned card, then?"

"Precisely. I could complete the work during the coming weeks, without neglecting my studies. You would receive the finished creation, and I would gain the opportunity to demonstrate my abilities."

Lucien considers the proposal.

"An interesting arrangement. I believe we could accommodate that."

He names a generous allowance for materials.

Emma's eyes widen almost imperceptibly.

"That would be entirely satisfactory."

They shake hands.

As you walk away, she turns toward you with an expression of barely suppressed triumph.

"Antonio. Do you have any idea what I can make with those ingredients?"

"Something impressive, I imagine."

"Something _magnificent_."

She pauses.

"And the best part is that I can continue my studies without interruption."

She gives you a delighted smile.

"I must admit, your advice was rather good."

"Emma, why not propose something we could work on together? We've already demonstrated that our combined talents can produce rather unusual results."

Emma looks at you thoughtfully.

"That is true."

"And between the two of us, we might be able to undertake something more ambitious without sacrificing quite so much time."

A mischievous smile spreads across her face.

"Fibonacci, are you suggesting that I share the glory?"

"Consider it a generous opportunity to benefit from my brilliance."

"How very charitable of you."

She laughs, then turns toward Lucien.

"Monsieur de Varenne, I wonder whether you might consider a slightly different arrangement."

She explains that the two of you have been experimenting with collaborative artificery, combining complementary techniques to produce unusual magical effects.

Lucien listens attentively.

"A joint project?"

"Precisely. Antonio is an exceptionally capable artificer, and we've discovered that our methods work rather well together."

She glances at you.

"When we manage not to argue over the details."

"An ongoing challenge," you agree.

Lucien smiles.

"Well, I certainly wouldn't object to meeting another promising scholar. Perhaps we could arrange a preliminary demonstration?"

Emma accepts enthusiastically.

When the conversation ends, she turns toward you with a satisfied smile.

"Well, partner. It seems we've acquired ourselves another project."

"You're welcome."

"Oh, don't look so smug. I haven't yet decided whether inviting you to share my research was an act of genius or a catastrophic lapse of judgment."

She slips her arm through yours.

"But I suppose we'll find out together."

the_offer.title: An Unexpected Opportunity

the_last_dance.text:
The conversation with Lucien concluded, you and Emma return to the main ballroom.

The orchestra has begun playing again, and the floor is filling with couples.

Emma seems unusually thoughtful as you walk together. Her evening has certainly turned out rather differently from what she expected.

Then she looks up at you and smiles.

"Well, Antonio. I believe our little expedition has been quite a success."

"You did make an impression."

"Naturally."

She pauses, then laughs softly.

"Although I must confess, I had almost forgotten about Lord de Varenne altogether. I was having rather too good a time."

You glance toward the dancers.

"Well, Delamain. The evening isn't over yet."

She follows your gaze.

"Another dance?"

"Unless you've had enough."

Emma looks at you for a moment, her expression warm and unusually unguarded.

"Not remotely."

She takes your hand.

"Come along, Antonio. I think I've done quite enough professional networking for one evening."

As you lead her back onto the dance floor, she adds with a mischievous smile:

"And besides, I haven't finished showing you off."

The orchestra swells, and the two of you disappear into the graceful whirl of dancers, leaving professional ambitions, influential patrons, and complicated futures to wait until morning.

For now, there is music.

And rather excellent company.
the_last_dance.title: One More Dance

text:
Tuesday evening. Your regular study session with Emma, an arrangement that has become something of a tradition. Tonight, however, there's an additional incentive.

Earlier that afternoon, Emma challenged you to solve a particularly difficult enchantment problem before she does. If you succeed, she'll give you one of her latest creations: an exceptionally fine blue card you've had your eye on for some time.

"And what happens if I win?" you asked.

"Well, Antonio, I thought it would be rather unkind to demand a prize from someone who has just suffered such a humiliating defeat."

The nerve of that woman.

You're still contemplating the many ways in which you intend to prove her wrong when you knock on her door.

Emma opens with her usual friendly smile. As usual, she's wearing a comfortable shirt. And, as usual, she's... oh.

Not quite as usual.

She's wearing shorts. Perfectly ordinary, comfortable indoor shorts. Admittedly, they appear to have been designed with rather extreme summer temperatures in mind.

{{smitten_reaction}}

"Antonio! Come in. I've prepared everything." She steps aside with an innocent smile. "I do hope you've brought your best ideas. You'll need them."

A quarter of an hour later, things are not going well.

Emma has made considerably more progress than you. She's settled sideways into her armchair, one foot resting on an armrest, her long legs crossed comfortably in front of her. Occasionally she stretches, shifts position, or leans over to consult a reference book, apparently without a care in the world.

You, meanwhile, have been staring at the same enchantment diagram for several minutes.

There is a perfectly respectable mathematical explanation for why the third resonance coefficient refuses to balance.

You would very much like to remember what it is.

Across the room, Emma makes another annotation. Then she glances at you over the top of her book.

"Everything all right, Fibonacci? You've been awfully quiet."

There's something suspiciously satisfied about that smile.

parameters.text:
"You know, Emma, you really ought to be careful. Aren't you afraid you'll catch cold dressed like that?"

Emma slowly lowers her book.

For a moment, she simply looks at you. Then a smile of pure, undisguised triumph spreads across her face.

"Oh? Is there something wrong with my clothes, Antonio?"

"Merely concerned for your well-being."

"How touching."

She rises from her chair with exaggerated dignity.

"Well, I must say, Fibonacci, I hadn't expected you to appoint yourself guardian of my wardrobe. This is my room, and I shall dress however I please."

She pauses, regarding you with a wicked little smile.

"Nevertheless, since your poor masculine constitution seems so terribly susceptible to distraction, I suppose I ought to make some allowances."

She gestures toward the door.

"Out you go. I'll change into something more suitable for your delicate sensibilities."

You have the distinct impression that this is not a concession.

You return your attention to the diagram.

The resonance coefficient. The secondary binding. The asymmetrical distribution of magical energy.

Slowly, the pieces fall into place.

Of course.

You make one final calculation, check it twice, and rise from your chair with your completed notes in hand.

Emma looks up, still wearing that infuriatingly satisfied little smile.

You approach her armchair and kneel before her.

"Emma, there's something I need to tell you."

Her smile vanishes.

"Oh."

For the first time this evening, she looks genuinely uncertain. She straightens in her chair, her eyes widening ever so slightly.

"Antonio, I..."

You take her hand.

"Something I've been trying to find the right words for all evening."

"Antonio!"

There's real alarm in her voice now. Her cheeks are turning pink.

You raise your sheet of calculations.

"I've solved it."

Silence.

Emma stares at the paper.

Then at you.

Then back at the paper.

"You..."

She snatches the sheet from your hand and examines the solution. Her expression passes through disbelief, intense concentration, reluctant admiration, and finally absolute outrage.

"You absolute scoundrel!"

You rise, looking enormously pleased with yourself.

"An elegant solution, wouldn't you say?"

Emma looks up at you, her cheeks still faintly pink.

"An appalling abuse of dramatic presentation, is what I'd call it."

"But mathematically sound?"

She studies the final equation one more time.

"Unfortunately."

Then she bursts out laughing.

"Oh, very well! You've earned your prize, you insufferable man."

She retrieves the promised blue card from her desk and presents it with an elaborate little bow.

"Congratulations, Fibonacci. A victory of questionable moral character, but a victory nonetheless."

You fix your attention firmly upon the enchantment problem.

For several minutes, you make respectable progress. You identify an error in the secondary binding and correct it, only to discover that the resulting resonance calculation produces an even more troublesome contradiction.

Across the room, Emma turns a page.

You glance up.

A mistake.

She catches your eye and smiles.

"Something interesting, Antonio?"

"Yes. Your third coefficient is wrong."

She examines her notes.

"Oh, you're quite right. Thank you."

With infuriating ease, she corrects the error and continues.

A moment later, she sets down her pen.

"There. I believe I've solved it."

You examine her work. The mathematics is impeccable.

Emma leans back with the air of a queen accepting tribute.

"Well, Fibonacci. It appears your powers of concentration require further development."

She glances down at her clothes, then back at you, a mischievous glint in her eyes.

"Perhaps I should remove any possible distractions before our next attempt."

title: An Unfair Advantage

variants.text:
Good heavens.

You'd thought yourself reasonably well acquainted with Emma's legs after that unfortunate episode at the ballet. Apparently, there are still considerable gaps in your education.

smitten_reaction.fallback:
You have always considered yourself quite capable of appreciating Emma's beauty without making a complete fool of yourself.

A sound principle. One which tonight appears to be undergoing a rather rigorous examination.

doubling_down.text:
Emma points toward the corridor.

"Honestly, Antonio, a little privacy. I'll call you when I'm ready."

You step outside, and the door closes behind you.

A few minutes pass. You hear some movement, a drawer opening, and what sounds suspiciously like a muffled laugh.

Then Emma calls out.

"You may come back in!"

You open the door.

Emma is once again comfortably installed in her armchair, her notes spread across her lap.

She has indeed changed. The shorts are gone, replaced by a pair of extraordinarily loose, comfortable trousers that cover her legs completely.

An admirable concession to modesty.

The shirt, however, is another matter.

It's a light, delicate linen garment, the sort one might wear on the hottest summer afternoon. The fabric is just translucent enough to make you suspect that Emma has interpreted your concerns with extraordinary selectivity.

She looks up, her cheeks faintly flushed, evidently struggling to keep a straight face.

"There. Is that better?"

She smooths the fabric over one knee with an air of complete innocence.

"I wouldn't want your academic performance to suffer on my account."

You look at her.

She looks at you.

This woman is enjoying herself far too much.

parameters.text:
"You know what, Emma? You're right."

She raises an eyebrow.

"Am I?"

"It's terribly warm in here."

You reach for the top button of your shirt.

Emma's smile falters.

"Antonio..."

You undo the button.

"I really ought to make myself more comfortable."

A second button.

"After all, as you so wisely pointed out, we're among friends."

Emma sits up abruptly.

"Fibonacci!"

You reach for a third.

She snatches a folded blanket from the arm of her chair and pulls it up in front of herself like a defensive rampart.

"All right! All right! That's quite enough!"

You stop, looking at her with exaggerated innocence.

"Something wrong with my clothes, Emma?"

For a moment, she glares at you over the blanket.

Then the absurdity of the entire situation catches up with her.

She starts laughing.

You follow almost immediately.

Within seconds, neither of you can maintain the slightest pretense of dignity. Emma collapses back into her chair, laughing so hard she has to wipe her eyes.

"Oh, Antonio! You wretched man!"

"Merely adapting to the climate."

"Of course you are!"

Eventually, she manages to recover enough to throw the blanket aside and retrieve her notes.

"Right. A truce. We have an enchantment to finish."

"And the competition?"

"Oh, forget the competition. At this rate, neither of us will graduate."

You settle beside her, still exchanging occasional smiles, and return to the problem. Without the ridiculous contest of distractions, the solution comes surprisingly quickly. Together, you work out an elegant way to stabilize the enchantment.

As you gather your notes, Emma gives you a warm, lingering smile.

"That was a rather enjoyable evening, Antonio."

"Despite my deplorable academic performance?"

"Entirely because of it, I suspect."

She pauses.

"And for the record, you looked perfectly respectable before you started undressing."

You take a slow breath and return to your calculations.

Whatever Emma has planned, you're determined not to give her the satisfaction.

The problem itself is fascinating. A complex interaction between two incompatible enchantments, requiring an unconventional redistribution of magical energy.

You begin to see the answer.

A few minutes later, you set down your pen.

Emma looks up.

"Giving up already?"

"Not quite."

You rise, carrying your completed calculations.

You make a determined attempt to concentrate.

Unfortunately, the mathematics is not cooperating, and neither is your opponent.

After another quarter of an hour, Emma finally sets down her pen.

"Finished."

You examine her work.

She's right.

Perfectly, infuriatingly right.

Emma regards you with a look of exquisite satisfaction.

"Well, Fibonacci, I believe that settles the matter."

"Your strategy was rather unconventional."

"My strategy was impeccable."

"I was referring to the enchantment."

"Naturally."

She smiles sweetly.

"Perhaps next Tuesday we'll try something simpler. I wouldn't want to strain you."

You collect your notes, already contemplating revenge.

Emma accompanies you to the door, looking altogether too pleased with herself.

"Good night, Antonio. And do get some rest. You seem unusually susceptible to fatigue lately."

doubling_down.title: Doubling Down

the_confession.text:
You approach Emma's armchair, your completed calculations carefully concealed beneath one hand.

She watches you with an expression of mild curiosity.

Then you kneel before her.

"Emma, there's something I need to tell you."

Her expression changes instantly.

"Oh."

She sits straighter.

"Antonio, what are you doing?"

"Something I've been meaning to do all evening."

Her cheeks begin to color.

"Antonio, I really don't think this is—"

You present your calculations with a flourish.

"I've solved it."

Emma blinks.

Once.

Twice.

Then she snatches the paper from your hand.

She studies the equations in silence, her expression growing steadily more incredulous.

Finally, she looks down at you.

"You absolute scoundrel."

You rise with a triumphant smile.

"An elegant solution, wouldn't you say?"

"An outrageously theatrical solution."

"But correct?"

She checks the final calculation.

A long sigh.

"Correct."

She rises, retrieves the promised blue card, and places it in your hand.

"There. Your prize. I hope you're satisfied."

"Immensely."

Emma folds her arms.

"Well, enjoy it while you can. Next Tuesday, I intend to be considerably less charitable."

She pauses, then smiles.

"And Antonio?"

"Yes?"

"If you ever kneel before me like that again, I expect an actual proposal."

You stare at her.

Her smile turns positively wicked.

"Of mathematical significance, naturally."
the_confession.title: A Startling Confession

text:
You're about to join the cafeteria queue when you hear a familiar voice behind you.

"Antonio! Surely you're not planning to eat _that_."

Emma approaches, eyeing the evening's offering with obvious suspicion.

"I was just heading home. Why don't you join me for dinner? I have some provisions, and I rather fancy cooking something myself for a change."

She smiles. "Unless you're particularly attached to boiled cabbage."

parameters.text:
"Well, when you put it like that..."

"Excellent. Come along, then. I promise you something considerably more interesting."

"Thanks, Emma, but I think I'll stay here tonight."

"As you wish." She glances toward the serving counter. "I admire your courage, if not your judgment."

She gives you a cheerful wave and heads off toward the village.

title: A Matter of Taste

dinner.text:
Emma's room is as you remember it: books everywhere, papers arranged in precarious towers, and just enough space on the little table for two plates. Tonight, however, the usual scholarly apparatus has been pushed aside to make room for a chopping board, a collection of vegetables, and a frying pan.

Emma rolls up her sleeves with the confidence of a woman about to perform a particularly elegant experiment.

"Now, let's see. This shouldn't be difficult."

Twenty minutes later, you are beginning to suspect otherwise.

The vegetables have been cut into wildly different sizes. Something at the bottom of the pan is turning an alarming shade of black, while the rest remains stubbornly raw. Emma studies the situation with increasing irritation, as though the ingredients are deliberately refusing to cooperate.

"How curious. I followed the recipe precisely."

You glance at the open cookbook. She has, in fact, skipped two steps and confused a teaspoon with a tablespoon.

"Emma, would you mind if I took over?"

She looks at you, genuinely affronted.

"Antonio, I am perfectly capable of preparing a simple meal."

A small cloud of smoke rises from the pan.

You both watch it.

"...Although I suppose a second opinion wouldn't hurt."

She reluctantly hands you the spoon.

You rescue what can be saved, clean the pan, and start again. Before long, the vegetables are sizzling pleasantly, the sauce has thickened, and the room is filled with a considerably more encouraging aroma.

Emma watches with undisguised fascination.

"Well. You seem remarkably practiced at this."

"I used to cook for my family. My parents were often ill, so somebody had to make dinner."

Her expression softens.

"I see. That must have been difficult."

You shrug. "You learn quickly when the alternative is going hungry."

Emma smiles faintly. "My parents always insisted I concentrate on my studies. They took care of practically everything else, even when they could scarcely afford the time. I suppose they rather spoiled me in that respect."

She considers the pan thoughtfully.

"Which explains why I can calculate the precise proportions of an alchemical compound, yet apparently cannot be trusted with an onion."

You offer her a taste of the sauce.

She takes it, pauses, and closes her eyes appreciatively.

"Oh, that's _good_."

Then she looks at you with a mixture of admiration and wounded professional pride.

"How thoroughly irritating."

Dinner turns out splendidly. You eat together at the little table, talking about classes, books, and the peculiar injustices of Academy life. Emma gradually abandons her injured dignity, and by the time the plates are nearly empty, she's laughing freely.

{{last_bite}}

parameters.title: Emma's upbringing
parameters.description: Emma's parents made considerable sacrifices to support her education, taking care of household responsibilities so she could devote herself to her studies. As a result, she's a surprisingly inexperienced cook.

dinner.title: A Matter of Taste

variants.text:
Only one delicious morsel remains on the serving plate.

You both notice it at precisely the same moment.

Emma reaches for it. So do you. Your forks meet with a delicate metallic _clink_.

"Antonio."

"Emma."

"I believe," she says gravely, "that as your hostess, I ought to have the final piece."

"And as your cook, I believe I've earned it."

She considers this argument. "A regrettably strong position."

You seize the opportunity, pick up the morsel with your fingers, and smile triumphantly.

"Victory."

Emma gives you a long, thoughtful look. Then a mischievous smile appears.

"Not quite."

She catches your wrist before you can withdraw your hand, gently draws it toward her, and, without breaking eye contact, takes the morsel delicately from between your fingers with her lips.

For a brief moment, you're too astonished to move.

Emma releases your hand, chews with exquisite composure, and smiles.

"Delicious. You really are an excellent cook, Antonio."

She looks entirely too pleased with herself.

last_bite.fallback:
There's barely a crumb left by the time you finish. Emma leans back in her chair, looking thoroughly satisfied.

"Well, Fibonacci. I have to concede that you've surpassed me in at least one field."

"Only one?"

"Don't get ambitious. I've already ordered a better cookbook."

She smiles over her empty plate.

"Although I may have to invite you back for further practical instruction."

card_gift.text:
As you prepare to leave, Emma retrieves a small card case from her desk.

"Before you go, there's something I'd like you to have."

She opens it, revealing several beautifully crafted cards.

"Choose one. Consider it a modest expression of gratitude for saving my dinner."

Her eyes narrow playfully.

"And not a word about this to Molly. I have a reputation to maintain."

title: A Rather Promising Match
text:
It's a pleasant evening at the inn. You and Emma have settled into a quiet corner for dinner, enjoying the rare luxury of having absolutely nothing important to discuss.

Molly has just left after spending a cheerful half-hour with you both. Emma watches her disappear through the door, a thoughtful smile on her lips.

"You know, Antonio, I've been meaning to ask you something."

She sets down her glass.

"Have you ever considered courting Molly?"

Well. That came out of nowhere.

"Don't look so astonished. She's a wonderful girl. Kind, funny, pretty, and considerably more sensible than either of us."

Emma pauses, then adds with a mischievous smile:

"Although I suspect she'd be quite happy with something less formal than a courtship, if that's more to your taste."

You raise an eyebrow.

"Emma Delamain. Are you trying to arrange my love life?"

"Someone ought to. You seem to be making remarkably little progress on your own."

She laughs, then grows a little more serious.

"Honestly, Antonio, I think she rather likes you. I can't promise anything, of course, but I doubt she'd turn you away if you asked."

She takes another sip of her drink, watching you with genuine curiosity.

"Well? What do you think?"

parameters.text:
"Well, I can't deny that Molly is lovely. And we do get along rather well."

Emma's face brightens.

"Precisely! I knew you weren't entirely hopeless."

"You're enjoying this far too much."

"Of course I am. Two of my favorite people, potentially making each other very happy? It's an excellent prospect."

She raises her glass with the satisfied air of a woman whose arrangements are progressing splendidly.

"Now, I shall leave you to work out the details. I refuse to conduct the entire courtship on your behalf."

You suspect she would rather enjoy doing exactly that.

You've been cutting the same piece of meat for an unusually long time.

Across the table, Emma's smile begins to fade. Perhaps she's wondering whether she's said something wrong.

Well. No point putting it off any longer.

"Emma... I'm afraid I have a rather unfortunate habit of pursuing hopeless, epic quests."

She raises an eyebrow.

"Oh?"

"You know the sort. A unique and wonderful treasure, guarded by a dragon far too powerful for me."

Emma looks puzzled.

"Antonio, what on earth are you—"

She stops.

For a moment, she simply studies you. Then something changes in her expression.

Your heart is beating so loudly you're half convinced she can hear it.

She understands.

"Antonio..." Her voice is quieter now. "You know, quests of that sort can take a very long time. And sometimes they lead nowhere at all."

"I know."

A faint blush colors her cheeks. Her eyes remain on yours, unusually serious.

Then, very slowly, the corner of her mouth curves upward.

"On the bright side," she says, "if the dragon eventually decides to eat you, I suspect you might rather enjoy it."

You nearly choke on your wine.

Emma laughs, and just like that, the unbearable tension dissolves.

"Really, Fibonacci. You ought to be more careful about the dangers you go looking for."

She returns to her meal, apparently quite composed.

Although, when you look up a moment later, you catch her watching you with a small, thoughtful smile.

"Thank you for your concern, Emma, but I think I'll manage my romantic affairs without professional assistance."

"Professional?" Emma looks delighted. "How flattering. I hadn't realized my advice carried such authority."

"Well, you do seem remarkably confident in your matchmaking abilities."

"Naturally. I have an excellent understanding of human nature."

"Then you'll understand that I prefer to make my own mistakes."

She laughs.

"Very well, Antonio. I shall respect your independence."

She takes another sip of wine, considering you over the rim of her glass.

"Although I reserve the right to say _I told you so_ when you make a spectacular mess of things."

"How generous."

"I thought so."

And with that, the subject is settled. At least until Emma discovers another opportunity to improve your life against your will.

title: A Tactical Diversion
text:
The market square is busy with its usual collection of merchants, shoppers, and people who appear to have nothing better to do than obstruct the passage of everyone else.

You're passing a bookstall when you spot Emma emerging from the crowd. Two young gentlemen in expensive, rather ostentatious clothes are following close behind her.

"Come now, my dear, surely you can spare us an afternoon!"

"I assure you, gentlemen, I cannot."

"Just one drink! You needn't be so difficult!"

Emma turns toward them, her smile becoming distinctly less friendly.

"For the third time, no. Good day."

She walks away. They follow.

Then she spots you.

Her expression changes instantly.

"Antonio!"

Before you can reply, she's striding toward you with a brilliant smile.

"Perfect timing," she whispers. "Play along."

She takes your hands, draws you close, and kisses you.

For a moment, you forget entirely about the market, the bookstall, and the existence of the human race.

You become vaguely aware of two disappointed voices nearby.

"Oh. Well, she might have mentioned..."

"Come on, let's go."

Their footsteps retreat.

Emma doesn't seem to notice.

Then, at last, she draws back.

She looks into your eyes for a brief moment before releasing your hands and turning to check that her admirers have disappeared.

"Excellent," she announces, recovering her usual composure. "That worked rather well."

You stare at her.

"Oh, don't look so scandalized, Antonio. It was a tactical diversion. Simple, elegant, and remarkably effective."

A small, mischievous smile appears.

"Besides, I knew I could count on your cooperation."

parameters.text:
You give her an extravagant bow.

"My lady, it is my sacred duty as your humble knight to defend you from unwanted suitors. Should you ever require such assistance again, you have only to call."

Emma laughs.

"How very gallant of you, Sir Antonio."

"And I must compliment you on your performance. Such dedication to your role!"

Emma blushes.

"You know me. I always do my best."

"Delamain, I entirely understand the strategic necessity of the kiss. A brilliant diversion, really."

Emma smiles with evident satisfaction.

"Naturally."

"Although there's one detail I find rather difficult to explain."

"Oh?"

"Wasn't the tongue a little excessive?"

Emma blushes, visibly amused, and suddenly finds something very interesting to look at on the other side of the square.

a_lucky_day.text:
Emma suddenly remembers something.

"Oh! Before I forget."

She opens her satchel and retrieves a small leather card case.

"I collected these from the artificery workshop this morning. Some experimental designs I've been working on. I was planning to show you later."

She opens the case, revealing three beautifully crafted cards.

"Here. Choose one. I'd like you to have it."

Then a thoroughly wicked smile spreads across her face.

"Antonio, I do hope you appreciate just how extraordinarily fortunate you are today."

She holds up one finger.

"First, the prettiest girl in town gives you a kiss."

A second finger.

"And then she presents you with a magnificent gift."

She sighs theatrically.

"Really, Fibonacci. I fear the rest of your life will be something of a disappointment by comparison."
a_lucky_day.title: Fortune Favors the Bold

title: The Devil's Garden
text:
Emma approaches you carrying a thick botanical encyclopedia, several folded maps, and the unmistakable expression of someone who has had a very interesting idea.

"Antonio. How would you feel about a little field research?"

Before you can answer, she unfolds a map of the Forest of Schlupak.

"I've been studying a rather remarkable species of mushroom. Schlupak's Thorncap. The flesh contains an extraordinarily potent defensive toxin. Properly distilled, it can be used to strengthen retaliatory enchantments, poisons, even direct damage spells."

She turns a page, revealing an illustration of a rather unpleasant-looking fungus.

"Unfortunately, it grows almost exclusively in the Forest of Schlupak. Which, as you may know, has a somewhat regrettable reputation."

A few days later, after a long walk beneath increasingly ancient trees, you find yourselves overlooking a sunken clearing. Thick clusters of dark crimson mushrooms grow among enormous tangled roots.

Emma kneels to examine the nearest specimens.

"Perfect. Exactly what we need."

She gestures toward a handful of mushrooms growing near the path, then toward a much larger cluster farther down the slope.

"Those near us are easily accessible. The others..." She studies the loose earth and the steep descent. "Well, we'd have to climb down. The ground doesn't look terribly stable."

She closes her notebook.

"Two specimens, safely gathered. Or four, if you're feeling ambitious. Your choice, Antonio."

parameters.text:
You gather the two nearest mushrooms while Emma prepares the protective containers. Their dark red caps release a faint, acrid smell as you carefully separate them from the roots.

"An excellent harvest," Emma declares, inspecting the specimens. "Not spectacular, admittedly, but perfectly respectable."

She glances down toward the larger cluster.

"Although I confess, there's something rather irritating about leaving perfectly good ingredients behind."

optionTemplates.text: Climb down for the larger harvest

parameters.text:
You carefully descend the slope, testing each foothold before committing your weight. Several stones tumble away beneath your boots, but you reach the lower roots safely.

Emma calls down instructions while you collect the mushrooms.

"Mind the red ones! No, not the mushrooms, the roots! The mushrooms are supposed to be red!"

Eventually, you scramble back up with four magnificent specimens.

Emma examines the contents of your bag, plainly delighted.

"Splendid work, Antonio. Four perfect specimens, and all your limbs still attached. A remarkably successful expedition."

The first few steps go well. Then a loose root gives way under your boot.

You slide down the slope in a spectacular shower of dirt, leaves, and small stones, coming to rest directly in the middle of the mushroom colony.

There is a distinctly unpleasant squelching sound.

By the time Emma helps you back onto solid ground, the mushrooms are thoroughly crushed and your clothing has acquired a remarkable collection of stains.

She surveys the devastation with scholarly dismay.

"Well. On the positive side, we've confirmed that the mushrooms release their toxins when subjected to physical trauma."

She looks at your ruined trousers.

"Rather enthusiastically, in fact."

title: The Dreaming Hollow
text:
"Antonio, do you remember our little expedition to the Forest of Schlupak?"

Emma produces a new map before you can reply.

"I've discovered something rather intriguing. There's an ancient hollow deep in the forest where two exceptionally rare magical substances can be found. I propose we investigate."

She looks at you with a smile.

"And this time, I've brought considerably better equipment."

Your second expedition takes you deeper into Schlupak than before. Eventually, the trees give way to an enormous hollow oak, its interior illuminated by an eerie blue-green light.

Inside, enormous translucent spheres hang suspended among the branches, slowly pulsing with pale violet light. Beneath them, clusters of delicate mushrooms release clouds of iridescent spores.

Emma stops dead.

"Oh, that's magnificent."

She approaches a floating sphere, examining it with obvious fascination.

"Schlupak Dreamspheres. Concentrated oneiric energy! Their magical properties are extraordinary. They're particularly useful for enchantments that manipulate the behavior of other spells and creatures."

Then she notices the mushrooms.

"And below them... Schlupak Spores. Equally valuable, but with very different properties. They enhance magical circulation and displacement. Excellent for drawing cards and returning summoned creatures to their owner's hand."

She begins unpacking her equipment.

"There's a complication, naturally."

She points toward the spheres.

"Disturbing a Dreamsphere causes the surrounding spores to disperse. But harvesting the spores destabilizes the spheres, making them dissolve."

Emma considers the problem for a moment, then shrugs.

"We can safely collect two specimens of either substance. Not both."

She looks at you.

"Well, Antonio? Which would be more useful for your next masterpiece?"

parameters.text:
You choose the floating spheres.

Emma nods approvingly and produces a curious glass instrument resembling a butterfly net designed by an astronomer.

"Excellent. Carefully, now. They're extremely sensitive to sudden movements."

Under her guidance, you capture two of the shimmering spheres. Their surfaces ripple gently as you lower them into protective containers.

The remaining spheres begin to fade, releasing a soft burst of light that scatters the spores throughout the hollow.

Emma holds up one of your acquisitions.

"Beautiful. Just think of the possibilities! Mesmerizing enemies, manipulating their actions, disrupting entire formations..."

Her expression grows thoughtful.

"Do remind me never to play against you without a suitable counterspell."

You indicate the clusters of mushrooms beneath the branches.

"The spores? Interesting."

Emma produces a small bellows and two sealed glass vessels.

"Very well. We shall have to be delicate. These things are extraordinarily sensitive to air currents."

She demonstrates a careful technique for gathering the spores without scattering them, then hands you the instrument.

After several minutes of painstaking work, both vessels are filled with shimmering powder.

Above you, the Dreamspheres begin to tremble, then dissolve into a gentle shower of violet sparks.

Emma examines your harvest with satisfaction.

"Excellent. With this much material, you could develop some truly remarkable circulation enchantments. Faster card recovery, magical displacement, perhaps even some interesting combinations."

She seals the vessels.

"And unlike certain other specimens we've encountered in this forest, these have made no attempt whatsoever to poison us."
