title: The Price of High Society
text:
You and Emma are leaving the Academy when a familiar voice calls after you.

"Emma! Antonio! Just the two people I was hoping to find."

Elsa Falkenstein approaches, looking particularly pleased with herself. She carries an elegant envelope, sealed with crimson wax.

"I'm hosting my birthday celebration at the Royal Pigeon Inn next Saturday. A proper reception, naturally. Music, dancing, an excellent dinner, and a rather distinguished guest list."

She hands Emma the envelope.

"I would very much like you to attend, Emma. Your little successes at the Academy have attracted quite a bit of attention lately. I think you'll find the company interesting, and I'm sure my guests will be delighted to meet you."

Emma studies the invitation, mildly surprised.

"How very gracious of you, Elsa."

"Naturally. And Antonio, I have a rather different role in mind for you."

Elsa's smile widens.

"I'm going to need an additional waiter."

There is a short silence.

"A waiter?" you repeat.

"Yes, darling. You do have experience in hospitality, don't you? And I've already arranged a proper uniform for you. White gloves, a splendid black coat, the works. You'll look positively magnificent."

Emma presses her lips together. You recognize the expression. She is making a considerable effort not to smile.

{{ invitation_terms }}

variants.text:
"Now, before you object," Elsa continues, "I believe we had an agreement. A certain little favor, in exchange for some rather valuable information about my brother."

Ah.

You remember that agreement. You remember expressing certain reservations about it, too.

Emma inclines her head.

"Quite right, Elsa. A promise is a promise."

"How refreshing! I knew I could count on you both."

Elsa looks positively radiant.

"And don't worry, Antonio. I assure you the uniform is of the very finest quality."

invitation_terms.fallback:
"Of course, I wouldn't dream of imposing on you without compensation," Elsa adds pleasantly. "Two hundred crowns each. For one evening. I think you'll agree that's a generous offer."

Emma raises an eyebrow.

"Two hundred each? That's rather extravagant for a birthday party."

"My dear Emma, I intend this to be an occasion people remember. Good company is worth paying for."

She turns toward you.

"Well, Antonio? What do you say?"

parameters.text:
"Well, a deal is a deal," you concede.

"Precisely!" Elsa claps her hands, delighted.

You turn toward Emma.

"Remind me, whose brilliant idea was it to owe Elsa a favor?"

Emma regards you with complete composure.

"I believe we agreed it was an excellent strategic decision at the time."

"Did we?"

"We obtained the information, didn't we?"

Elsa watches the exchange with evident satisfaction.

"Oh, this is going to be such a lovely evening."

"Two hundred crowns for an evening's work? Very well. You have yourself a waiter."

"Splendid!" Elsa beams. "I knew you'd be reasonable."

Emma looks at you with amused disbelief.

"Antonio Fibonacci, bought for two hundred crowns. I shall remember this."

"Coming from someone who just accepted two hundred crowns for attending a party, that's rather rich."

"Ah, but I'm attending as a guest. You're serving drinks."

Elsa looks from one to the other, clearly enjoying herself.

"Wonderful. Now, about your measurements..."

"Thank you, Elsa, but I think I'll decline. Two hundred crowns is tempting, but I didn't come to the Academy to spend my evenings serving drinks."

Elsa looks briefly disappointed.

"Oh, what a pity. I was so looking forward to seeing you in the uniform."

"I'm sure you were."

Emma gives you an approving glance.

"A perfectly reasonable decision, Antonio. Though I confess, I'm a little disappointed myself."

"About the money?"

"About the uniform, naturally."

Elsa sighs.

"Well, I'll simply have to find someone else. Emma, darling, I do hope you'll still come."

Emma considers the invitation.

"Why not? It sounds like an interesting evening."

Elsa brightens at once, and the two young women begin discussing the guest list, leaving you with the uncomfortable realization that your refusal has deprived you of precisely one thing: an opportunity for Emma to laugh at your expense.

birthday_party.text:
The Royal Pigeon Inn has been transformed for the occasion. Chandeliers glitter above elegantly dressed guests, a small orchestra plays near the windows, and liveried servants glide between the tables bearing silver trays of delicacies.

Elsa has spared no expense. To her credit, the result is magnificent.

You, meanwhile, are standing in a servants' room, contemplating your reflection in a mirror.

The uniform is magnificent too, in its own way. A stiff black tailcoat, a brilliant white waistcoat, an enormous bow tie, immaculate white gloves, and a collar so high that turning your head has become a complicated operation.

You look like a penguin that has inherited a title.

The head waiter inspects you, adjusts your bow tie by a fraction of an inch, and hands you a silver tray.

"Sparkling wine. The ladies at the table by the window."

You take the tray and make your way through the reception.

There, seated together in elegant evening dresses, are Emma and Molly. The two friends are enjoying themselves enormously, laughing over some private conversation.

Emma notices you first.

Her expression freezes.

Her eyes travel slowly from your polished shoes to the tails of your coat, then upward to the magnificent bow tie.

She presses a hand to her mouth.

Molly turns to see what has caught her attention.

"Oh! Antonio! You look so..."

Molly stops, searching desperately for a suitable adjective.

"...professional!"

That does it.

Emma lets out a small, strangled sound. She attempts to disguise it as a cough, then as a sip from her glass, but the effort is hopeless. Her shoulders begin to shake.

"Emma," you say with as much dignity as your collar permits, "may I offer you some sparkling wine?"

She tries to answer. She truly does.

"Thank you, Antonio, that's very..."

Her eyes meet yours.

"...very..."

And then she loses the battle entirely.

She bursts into helpless laughter, bending forward with one hand over her face. Molly, caught between sympathy for you and the contagious absurdity of the situation, begins giggling too.

For perhaps half a minute, Emma is quite incapable of speech.

At last, she manages to recover enough composure to accept a glass.

"Oh, Antonio!" She wipes a tear from the corner of her eye. "Forgive me. It's just... that bow tie! And the way you're standing!"

"Madam," you reply stiffly, "I am merely endeavoring to provide the highest standard of service."

This proves to be a serious mistake.

Emma collapses into laughter again.

Molly reaches across the table to pat your hand sympathetically.

"I think you look very handsome, Antonio. Really!"

"Thank you, Molly."

Emma raises her glass, still struggling to contain herself.

"To Antonio Fibonacci," she declares, "the most distinguished gentleman ever to carry a tray!"

You give an elaborate bow, to the evident delight of both ladies, and retreat with what remains of your dignity.

Across the room, Elsa watches the scene with a satisfied little smile. Her party is going splendidly.

And judging by the laughter still coming from the table by the window, it is certainly going to be remembered.
birthday_party.title: A Most Distinguished Waiter

title: An Evening's Entertainment
text:
The Old Monk Inn is unusually lively tonight. Its common room is crowded with merchants, travelers, and townsfolk enjoying their supper. Above the cheerful clatter of glasses and conversation, a violin is playing.

And playing beautifully.

You follow the music toward the far end of the room, where a young woman stands beside the fireplace, her bow moving effortlessly across the strings. The melody is lively and intricate, drawing delighted smiles from the guests.

Emma Delamain.

Of course. Is there _anything_ this woman cannot do?

She finishes with a magnificent flourish, and the room bursts into applause. Several coins find their way into a little wooden bowl beside her chair.

Emma accepts the appreciation with a graceful bow. Then she spots you.

"Antonio! What a pleasant surprise." Her eyes brighten with an idea. "Tell me, do you have any plans for the evening?"

Before you can answer, she gestures toward the crowded room.

"The innkeeper lets me perform here occasionally. The pay isn't magnificent, but the tips are respectable, and apparently the guests prefer my violin to his nephew's bagpipes."

She glances at the growing crowd.

"Unfortunately, I seem to have become rather popular tonight. Would you care to make yourself useful? I could do with someone to collect requests, carry drinks, and ensure my admirers remember where to leave their coins."

She offers you an innocent smile.

"Consider it an opportunity to participate in the arts."

parameters.title: Music and livelihood
parameters.description: Emma is a virtuoso violinist, the result of years of dedicated practice. She occasionally performs at the Old Monk Inn to earn money for her living expenses. Unlike most Academy students, she cannot rely on family wealth and must work alongside her studies.

parameters.text:
"Very well. I've worked in an inn before. How difficult can it be?"

"Splendid! I knew I could rely on your extensive professional qualifications."

She presses a serving tray into your hands.

"Now, the gentleman in the green coat has requested something cheerful, the merchant by the window insists on a traditional ballad, and the table near the stairs has ordered another round of wine."

She pauses.

"Oh, and Antonio? Do try not to accept any requests for bagpipes."

"I think I'll leave the professional entertainment to you. Someone has to appreciate it from the audience."

"A wise decision. I should hate to discover that you have hidden musical talents as well. My professional reputation might never recover."

You find a seat and enjoy the performance over a mug of ale. Emma plays magnificently, moving from lively dances to tender ballads, occasionally catching your eye with a small, conspiratorial smile.

When the applause finally dies away, she gives you a theatrical bow.

"Thank you for your patronage, Signor Fibonacci. Your contribution to the arts has been invaluable."

after_performance.text:
The evening proves unexpectedly entertaining. You carry drinks, collect musical requests, and persuade a particularly enthusiastic merchant that standing directly in front of the violinist to declare his admiration is not strictly necessary.

Meanwhile, Emma performs with astonishing skill. She moves effortlessly between solemn melodies and lively dances, captivating the entire room. Even the innkeeper abandons his accounts to listen.

At one point, a rather tipsy gentleman insists that he knows a traditional dance from his homeland. Emma obligingly begins playing, and you watch him demonstrate something resembling a goose attempting to escape a sack.

Emma manages to finish the tune without laughing.

Barely.

By the time the last guests depart, the wooden bowl is overflowing with coins. Emma sits beside you at an empty table and begins counting, arranging the money into neat little stacks.

"Well! That was considerably more profitable than expected."

She separates a generous portion of the earnings, then retrieves a card from the little case beside her violin.

"Now, Antonio, you've earned your share. One hundred gold, if you'd prefer something practical."

She places the card next to the coins.

"Or this. A spare creation of mine. Rather a clever little enchantment, if I say so myself."

She smiles.

"And I generally do."

parameters.text:
"I'll take the money, thank you. I've acquired a rather expensive habit of attending the Academy."

"An appalling habit. I suffer from precisely the same affliction."

Emma pushes the coins toward you.

"One hundred gold, as promised. You've earned every piece."

She gathers the remaining coins into her purse, looking thoroughly satisfied.

"An excellent evening's work, Fibonacci. Perhaps we should go into business together."

"I'll take the card. Money comes and goes, but a good enchantment is worth keeping."

Emma looks pleased.

"An intelligent choice. Although I should point out that money has the considerable advantage of being accepted by bakers."

She hands you the card, watching with quiet satisfaction as you examine her work.

"I made that one last term. It served me rather well, but I've since improved upon the design."

"You're giving me your discarded experiments?"

"My _surplus masterpieces_, Antonio. There's a difference."

She smiles.

"Do take good care of it."

after_performance.title: A Profitable Evening

title: A Standing Engagement
text:
"Antonio! Just the man I was looking for."

Emma approaches you with a particularly satisfied expression. Evidently, something has gone her way.

"Remember our little musical enterprise? Well, I've received an offer from the Old Monk Inn. They want me to perform every Friday evening. Regular pay, generous tips, and apparently an audience with excellent taste."

She pauses, smiling.

"Naturally, I accepted. But I'd much rather concentrate on the violin than spend half the evening chasing drunken merchants for their unpaid bills."

She regards you thoughtfully.

"So, what do you say to making our partnership official? Every Friday evening, a few hours of honest work, and we divide the earnings. I provide the artistic talent, you provide the indispensable logistical support."

Her smile turns mischievous.

"An exceptionally fair arrangement, wouldn't you agree?"

parameters.text:
"Why not? We made a pretty good team last time."

"Excellent! I knew you were a man of sound judgment."

Emma looks delighted.

"Friday evenings, then. The Old Monk Inn. I'll speak to the innkeeper and make the arrangements."

She begins to leave, then turns back.

"Oh, and Antonio? If anyone asks, you're my _manager_. It sounds so much more distinguished than 'the fellow who carries the drinks.'"

job.name: Musical Evenings with Emma
job.description: Every Friday evening at the Old Monk Inn: Emma provides the violin, you provide the logistical support.

parameters.text:
"I'm afraid I can't commit to every Friday evening. Academy life keeps me busy enough already."

"Of course. A demanding scholarly career must come first."

Emma nods, entirely untroubled.

"I'll find someone else to help. Perhaps a young man with fewer ambitions and a greater appreciation for carrying trays."

She gives you a teasing smile.

"Still, you must come and listen sometime. I promise not to charge you admission."

text:
Your third artificery lesson is progressing remarkably well. You've arranged your ingredients, prepared your pigments, and even managed to follow most of the professor's instructions. At this rate, you might produce something almost respectable.

Then your elbow catches a jar.

A cascade of shimmering blue powder spills across the workbench, mixing with your carefully prepared ingredients. You grab for a cloth, knock over a second jar, and watch in horror as the entire mixture begins to glow.

There is a sharp pop, a flash of blue light, and the unmistakable smell of burnt cinnamon.

When the smoke clears, a perfectly formed card lies in the middle of the table.

You pick it up cautiously. The enchantments woven into its surface are unlike anything you've seen before: intricate, powerful, and somehow perfectly balanced.

The professor approaches, examines your creation, and falls silent.

"Fibonacci. How exactly did you achieve this?"

An excellent question. One you would very much like to know the answer to yourself.

"Remarkable," the professor murmurs. "Quite remarkable. You must document your procedure."

Yes. Of course. Your procedure.

You glance at the empty jars, the stained workbench, and the smoking remains of your notes.

This could be difficult.
title: Happy Little Accident

text:
Professor Lombard is about to start her class when the classroom door opens. The Academy's administrator enters, carrying a large ledger and looking as though he has come to collect money. You instinctively check your purse.

"Ah, excellent timing!" Lombard exclaims. "Ladies and gentlemen, a little announcement before we start."

The administrator adjusts his spectacles.

"The Academy's first league season of the academic year begins today. As is tradition, each student shall face every other student exactly once in an official match. Victories will earn points toward the league standings, and the student finishing first shall receive a prize in recognition of their achievement."

That gets everyone's attention.

"The league is an important part of your education," Glützenbaum adds enthusiastically. "A chance to test your creations, exercise your strategic abilities, and demonstrate your progress. And remember, you will be competing with the very cards you craft and enchant during your studies!"

Around the room, the reactions are decidedly mixed. Emma sits a little straighter, her green eyes bright with unmistakable determination. Beside her, Vaiana yawns extravagantly, apparently finding the prospect of an entire season of competition rather exhausting. Ousmane slowly twirls his magnificent moustache, contemplating the announcement with the serene confidence of a general surveying a battlefield.

Molly, meanwhile, looks rather less enthusiastic. She glances around at her classmates, then down at her modest deck, visibly calculating just how many defeats she might be expected to endure.

"Your first official matches may begin this afternoon," the administrator concludes. "Choose your opponents, prepare your decks, and may the best artificer win."

"Splendid!" Lombard claps his hands. "Nothing like a little healthy competition to encourage academic excellence! Do try to remain on speaking terms with one another."

You survey your fellow students. Several are already exchanging challenging looks.

Apparently, your education is about to become considerably more interesting.
